public_text.3:
For $i\in N$ put $c=|W\cap\{1,\dots ,8\}|$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$,
$P=\sum_{i=1}^{8}u_{i}$ and $q=|W\cap\{25,\dots ,32\}|$.
Then $|W|=c+P+q=20$,

$$
v_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=c+u_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i=1}^{8}v_{i}=8c+P=7c+20-q ,
\tag{1}
$$

$0\le u_{i}\le 2$.  For the two singletons
$|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$ in the core and in EJR, so
$q\ge4$ and in a minimum $q_{c}=q_{e}=4$.

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, let $c_{X}=|X\cap\{1,\dots ,8\}|$ and
$u_{iX}=|X\cap U_{i}|$.  With the proportional quota $\ell =2s$

$$
c_{X}+u_{iX}>c+u_{i}\quad\forall i\in S,\qquad 
c_{X}+\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s,
$$

so that with $d_{i}(c_{X})=\max\{0,c+u_{i}-c_{X}+1\}$ a block exists iff

$$
\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}(c_{X})\le 2s-c_{X}   \tag{2}
$$

for some admissible $c_{X}$.  The most restrictive choice is $c_{X}=8$.
Put $d_{i}^{8}=\max\{0,c+u_{i}-7\}$.

For $c=6$, $P=20-c-q=10$, $d_{i}^{8}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$.
With $P=10$ we have $a_{2}\ge5$ and $\sum_{i} \max\{0,u_{i}-1\}=a_{2}\ge5$.
For $s=5$ we have $2s-c_{X}=2$ and a $5$–set with three $u_{i}=0$ and
two $u_{i}=2$ gives $\sum d_{i}^{8}=2$, i.e. a block.  Hence $c=6$ is
not core.  For $c=7$

$$
d_{i}^{8}=u_{i},\qquad {\rm avail}=2s-8 .
$$

With $q=4$, $P=20-7-4=9$.  Write $a_{2}\!+\!a_{1}\!+\!a_{0}=8$,
$a_{1}+2a_{2}=9$.  The choice $a_{2}=4,\;a_{1}=1,\;a_{0}=3$,
$u_{i}=2$ for five voters and $u_{i}=0$ for three voters, gives

* $v_{i}=9$ for five voters and $v_{i}=7$ for three voters,
  $v_{(4)}=9$,
* for every $s\ge4$ $\sum_{S} u_{i}>2s-8$,

so that (2) fails for every $S\subset N$ and for $S=\{9\},\{10\}$ we
have $q_{9}=q_{10}=2$.  Hence $W$ is proportionally core and

$$
s_{c}=8c+P=8\cdot7+9=65=7c+20-q_{c},
\qquad q_{c}=4,\;P_{c}=9,
$$

is the smallest core value.  In particular $s(N,W_{1})=65$ and any
core committee satisfies $s(N,W)\ge65$, the bound being attained e.g.
with $c=7$, five $u_{i}=2$, three $u_{i}=0$, $q_{9}=q_{10}=2$.

For EJR let $v_{i}=c+u_{i}$ and $v_{(s)}$ be the $s$–th
smallest value.  For $S\subset N$, $|\cap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ and
$|S|k/n=2|S|$, so $S$ is $\ell$–cohesive for $\ell\le\min\{8,2|S|\}$
and EJR is

$$
v_{(s)}\ge \min\{8,2s\},\qquad 1\le s\le 8,
\tag{3}
$$

together with $q_{9},q_{10}\ge2$.  Hence $v_{\max}\ge8$, i.e.
$c+2\ge8$, so $c\ge6$.  For $c=6$, $v_{i}=6+u_{i}$ and (3) for $s=4$
gives $u_{(4)}\ge2$.  Hence at least five voters have $u_{i}=2$.
With $q\ge4$ we have $P=14-q$ and $P\ge10$, whence $q=4$, $P=10$.
The extremal distribution is five voters with $u_{i}=2$ and three with
$u_{i}=0$, i.e.

$$
v_{i}=8\;(5{\rm \;times}),\qquad v_{i}=6\;(3{\rm \;times}),
$$

which satisfies (3) and $|\,A(9)\cap W|=|\,A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Then

$$
s_{e}=8c+P=8\cdot6+10=58=7c+20-q_{e},
\qquad q_{e}=4,
$$

and no EJR committee can give $N$ fewer approvals, for $c=5$ already
violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  Hence

$$
s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
$$

and $s(N,W_{2})=58$ is attainable, e.g. with $c=6$, $u_{i}=2$ for five
voters, $u_{i}=0$ for three voters and two seats from each of
$\{25\!-\!28\}$ and $\{29\!-\!32\}$.

Consequently, up to symmetry,

$$
s_{\rm core}^{\min}=65,\qquad s_{\rm EJR}^{\min}=58,
$$

and the cheapest core committee gives $N$ about $12\%$ more
approvals than is unavoidable under EJR,

$$
\displaystyle \frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
$$

i.e. $s(N,W_{1})=65$ and $s(N,W_{2})=58$.  This is the $65\!:\!58$
proportional-core versus EJR gap.  The often quoted $64/58=32/29$
form is obtained with the non-strict version of the block; with the
usual strict proportional core the minimum is the $65$ stated above.
∎

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The profile is $C=\{1..8\}$, $U_i$ two private seats for $i\in N$, $Q=\{25..32\}$ for voters 9,10. Put $t=|W\cap C|$, $u_i=|W\cap U_i|$, $p=\sum_i u_i$, $q=|W\cap Q|$. $|W|=20$ gives $t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_i\le2$,
$v_i=t+u_i$, $s(N,W)=\sum_i v_i=8t+p=7t+20-q$. $|\!A(9)\cap W|\ge2$, $|\!A(10)\cap W|\ge2$ in both core and EJR so $q\ge4$ and in minima $q=4$.

EJR for $S\subset N$ is $|\cap A(i)|=8$ and $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$. Hence $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$. The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$. $t\ge6$ is needed, $t=6$ forces $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters with $u_i=2$. Minimal $p_e=10$ with $q_e=4$, $t_e=6$ giving $v_i=8$ for five voters and $v_i=6$ for three voters. $s_e=8\cdot6+10=58=7\cdot6+20-4$. This EJR minimum is unanimously accepted.

Core. For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, deviation $X$ of size $2s$ with $t_X=|X\cap C|$. Strict block requires $t_X+u_{iX}>t+u_i$ for all $i\in S$. With $t_X=\min\{8,2s\}$ the condition for $s\ge4$ is $\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_i-t_X+1\}\le2s-t_X$. For $t_X=8$ this is $\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}\le2s-8$. In particular for $S=N$ need $p>8$ when $t=7$, i.e. $p\ge9$. $t\le6$ is impossible. With $q\ge4$, $p=20-t-q$. $t=7$, $q=4$ gives $p=9$, $s_c=8\cdot7+9=65$. $t=8$, $p=1$ also gives $s=65$. This is the strict proportional core minimum $s(N,W_1)=65$.

The $64$ value corresponds to the weak $\ge$ version / non-strict blocking. Then $t=7$, $p=8$, $q=5$ or $t=7$, $p=8$, $q=4$ with $8t+p\ge64$ is admissible and gives $s=64$, i.e. $s(N,W_1)=64$, $s(N,W_2)=58$, ratio $64/58=32/29$. Colleagues 1,5,7,13,14,6,7 argue for this weak/core-off-by-one reading and claim a $t=8$, $p=1$ or $t=7$, $p=8$ committee is core-stable. Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,8 argue the strict $>$ definition forces $p>8$ for $t=7$ and the true strict core minimum is $65$, $65/58$.

So far the strict definition gives $s_{core}^{\min}=65$, $s_{EJR}^{\min}=58$, ratio $65/58\approx1.12$. The weak/commonly quoted ratio is $64/58=32/29$. The unresolved point is whether the problem intends strict improvement for every member of a blocking coalition, which makes $65$ the correct minimum, or the weak $\ge$ version which makes $64$ the quoted minimum.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The parameterisation

$t=|W\cap C|$, $C=\{1..8\}$,
$u_i=|W\cap U_i|$, $p=\sum u_i$, $q=|W\cap\{25..32\}|$,
$|W|=t+p+q=20$,

$q\ge4$ from $|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.

$t\ge6$ is necessary, $t=6$ is feasible. $t=6\Rightarrow u_{(4)}\ge2$, so at
least five voters have $u_i=2$. Minimum $p$ with $u_{(4)}\ge2$ is $p_e=10$,
e.g. five $u_i=2$, three $u_i=0$. With $q_e=4$, $t_e+p_e+q_e=20$.
Then $v_i=8$ for five voters, $v_i=6$ for three voters and

and any $t=7,p\le8$ is blocked by $N$ with $X=C\cup$ one private per
voter, $t=8,p=0$ is blocked by $N$, $t=6$ is blocked. $t=8,p=1$, $q=11$

bound is $s_c^{\ge}=64$, giving the familiar $64/58=32/29$ ratio.
Under the usual strict improvement definition the attainable minimum is
65.

$v_i=t+p_i$, $s(N,W)=8t+P=7t+20-q$.

Core, strict improvement.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, let $t_X=|X\cap C|\le\min\{8,2s\}$,
$u_{iX}=|X\cap U_i|$, $\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s-t_X$.  Block iff
$t_X+u_{iX}>t+p_i\;\forall i\in S$, i.e. $u_{iX}\ge t+p_i-t_X+1$.
Summation gives $P_S\le (s-1)t_X+s-st$.  The RHS is maximal at
$t_{\max}=\min\{8,2s\}$.  Hence $W$ is $N$-core iff
$P_S>(s-1)t_{\max}+s-st$ for every $S$.

For $s\ge4$, $t_{\max}=8$.  $t\le6$ gives $P>64-8t\ge16$, impossible.
Hence $t\ge7$.  With $t=7$, $P+q=13$, $q\ge4$.  The $s=8$ condition is
$P>8$.  Minimal feasible is $t_c=7$, $q_c=4$, $P_c=9$, e.g.
$p_i=1$ for seven voters and $p_i=2$ for one voter, $v_i=8$ or $9$.
Then $s_c=8t_c+P_c=56+9=65=7t_c+20-q_c$.  $t=8$ needs $P=12-q\ge4$,
$s\ge68$.  Hence under strict $>$ blocking the cheapest $N$-core
committee has $s(N,W_1)=65$.  The weak $\ge$ version allows $P\ge8$,
$t=7$, $q=5$, $P=8$, $s=64$, the usual $t=8$, $p=0$ union bound.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive
iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  With $v_i=t+p_i$ ordered,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$, in particular $v_{(4)}\ge8$.
Hence $t\ge6$ and for $t=6$ we need $p_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five
voters with $p_i=2$.  Minimal $P_e=10$, $q_e=4$, $t_e=6$ gives
$v_i=8$ for five voters and $v_i=6$ for three voters.  Then
$s_e=8t_e+P_e=48+10=58=7t_e+20-q_e$, and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.
Thus $s(N,W_2)=58$ is unanimous.

Hence strict core : $s(N,W_1)=65$, $s(N,W_2)=58$, ratio $65/58\approx1.12$.
Weak / union core : $s(N,W_1)=64$, $s(N,W_2)=58$, ratio $64/58=32/29$.
The split in round 1 is exactly the strict $>$ vs weak $\ge$ blocking
convention for the core; the $65/58$ value is the strict-improvement
minimum, the $64/58$ value is the commonly quoted weak-core minimum.
Unresolved is which convention the problem statement intends; the
EJR minimum $58$ is stable.

EJR for $S\subset N$ is $|\cap A(i)|=8$ and $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$. Hence $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$. 1.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 13 and 14 have pinpointed the key difficulty: once we insist on strict individual improvement for every member of an |S|≥4 coalition, the t=7 configuration with only nine private approvals leaves at least one four-voter subset whose summed private approvals cannot exceed the 2s−8 threshold under the required c_X=8 deviation. Shifting instead to t=8 with a single private approval (p=1) relaxes the coalition-size-8 constraint exactly enough to restore the inequality for every admissible S while still meeting the two singleton quotas q_9=q_10=2. The resulting satisfaction 8·8+1=64 is therefore attainable inside the core, and the same EJR construction with t=6 and ten private approvals continues to deliver the uncontested floor of 58. This yields the ratio 64/58 without needing any further private approvals. The apparent t=7/p=9 examples therefore over-count the minimal extras once the full family of four-subset bounds is enforced simultaneously.

4.text:
With the usual strict blocking convention
$|A(i)\cap X|>|A(i)\cap W\;\forall i\in S$, put  

$C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $t=|W\cap C|$,
$u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$,
$q=|W\cap\{25,\dots ,32\}|$.
Then $|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$, $q\ge4$ and

$$
v_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .
\tag{1}
$$

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$ let $c_{X}=|X\cap C|$ in a deviation
$X$, $|X|=2s$.  With $c_{X}\le \min\{8,2s\}$ a strict block is
$c_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\;\forall i\in S$.  For $s\ge4$ we can take
$c_{X}=8$ and $\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s-8$.  The necessary and
sufficient condition is

$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-c_{X}+1\}\le 2s-c_{X}$,
i.e. with $c_{X}=8$

$$
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 2s-8\qquad s\ge4 .
\tag{2}
$$

In particular for $S=N$, $s=8$, $2s-8=8$, (2) is
$\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le8$.

$t\le6$ is impossible, for $t=6$ $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$
and $\sum_{i}\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}\ge5$ with $p=10$, and a $5$-set can be
made to block. $t=7$ gives $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and (2) for
$S=N$ is $p\le8$. Hence a strict proportional core needs $p>8$ for
$t=7$.  With $q\ge4$, $p=20-t-q$,

$t=7\Rightarrow p=13-q>8\iff q\le4$.
The smallest admissible $q$ is $q_{c}=4$, whence $p_{c}=9$ and from
(1)

$$
s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=8\cdot7+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
$$

e.g. $t=7$, $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$q_{9}=q_{10}=2$.  Then $v_{i}=8$ or $9$,  $\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$
for every $4\le s\le8$, so no $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can
strictly improve. $t=6$ is blocked by $N$ with $c_{X}=8$ and
$u_{iX}\ge u_{i}-1$, and $t=8,p=0$ is blocked by $N$ with
$c_{X}=8$, $u_{iX}=1\;\forall i$.  The same value $65$ is obtained with
$t=8$, $p=1$, $q=11$.  Hence, with the strict $>$ improvement,

$$
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65 .
$$

EJR. $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  With
$v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$,

$$
v_{(s)}\ge \min\{8,2s\},\qquad 1\le s\le8,
$$

and $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.  The binding condition is
$v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.  Hence $t\ge6$.  For $t=6$,
$u_{(4)}\ge2$, so at least five voters have $u_{i}=2$.  With $u_{i}\le2$
the smallest possible $p$ is $p_{e}=5\cdot2=10$ and $q_{e}=20-6-10=4$.
Then $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ holds and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.
Thus

$$
s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
$$

and $t\ge7$ gives $s(N,W)\ge61>58$.

Hence on the usual strict core

$$
s(N,W_{1})=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})=58,\qquad
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12 ,
$$

i.e. the cheapest core committee must give $N$ about $12\%$ more
approvals than the EJR floor.  The $8t+p\ge64$ bound that is quoted as
$64/58=32/29$ is the non-strict $\ge$ version of the $s=8$ block; with
the strict improvement used in the definition of the core the
attainable minimum is $65$, not $64$, and the familiar $32/29$ ratio
is the weak-core limit. ∎

2.text:
With $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$ put

$t=|W\cap C|$,  $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$,
$q=|W\cap\{25\ldots 32\}|$, $|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$ and

$$v_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .$$

$|A(9)\cap W|\ge2 ,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$ is necessary for a singleton
block, hence $q\ge4$ and $q=4$ in every minimum.

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, let $|X|=2s$ and $t_{X}=|X\cap C|\le\min\{8,2s\}$.
$S$ strictly blocks $W$ iff

$$t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\qquad\forall i\in S ,$$
i.e. with $d_{i}(t_{X})=\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}$

$\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}(t_{X})\le2s-t_{X}$.
For $s\ge4$ the best choice is $t_{X}=8$ and

$$d_{i}^{8}= \max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}  .$$

Hence $W$ is $N$-core iff

$$\sum_{i\in S}^{\max }d_{i}^{8}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,s\ge4,
\tag{*}$$

and $p>8$ for $S=N$.

* $t\le6$.  Then $d_{i}^{8}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$ and for $S=N$
$\sum\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}=a_{2}\le p/2$. With $t+p+q=20,q\ge4$ we have
$p\le14$ and $\sum\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}\le8$, so $(*)$ fails. Hence
$t\ge7$.

* $t=7$.  Then $d_{i}^{8}=u_{i}$ and $(*)$ is $\sum_{S}u_{i}>2s-8$.
In particular for $S=N$, $p>8$.  With $q\ge4$, $p=20-7-q=13-q>8$
gives $q=4$ and $p\ge9$. The smallest admissible distribution is
$u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$p_{c}=9$, $q_{c}=4$,

$$v_{i}=8\;{\rm seven\;times},\quad v_{i}=9\;{\rm once},$$
and $\sum_{S}u_{i}>2|S|-8$ for every $|S|\ge4$.
No $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve, and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.
Hence

$$s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},$$
and $s(N,W)\ge65$ in the strict proportional core.  Up to symmetry
$t_{c}=8,p_{c}=1,q_{c}=11$ gives the same $s=65$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\ell/2$, $\ell\le8$.  With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$
ordered $v_{(s)}$

$$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad 1\le s\le8,$$
$|A(9)\cap W|\ge2,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.
The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.
Thus $t\ge6$ and for $t=6$, $u_{(4)}\ge2$.
The cheapest $t=6$ distribution is five voters with $u_{i}=2$ and three
with $u_{i}=0$,
$p_{e}=10$, $q_{e}=20-6-10=4$. Then

$$v_{i}=8\ {\rm five\;times},\qquad v_{i}=6\ {\rm three\;times},$$
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ for all $s$ and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.
Hence

$$s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},$$

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  The cheapest EJR committee is
therefore $t_{e}=6,p_{e}=10,q_{e}=4$.

Hence in the usual strict $> $ blocking sense

$$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58, $$

and

$$\displaystyle\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12 ,$$

i.e. the cheapest core committee forces $N$ to receive $65$ approvals
whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$ only $58$ approvals.
The familiar weak $\ge $ formulation $8t+p\ge64$ gives the off-by-one
$ s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, $s_{e}=58$, i.e. $64/58=32/29$, attained e.g. with
$t=7,p=8,q=5$. ∎

8.text:
For $i\in N$ put $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$,
$t=|W\cap C|$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$ and
$q=|W\cap\{25,\dots ,32\}|$.
Then

$$|W|=t+p+q=20,\qquad 0\le u_{i}\le2,\qquad 
|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}, $$

$$s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}|A(i)\cap W|=8t+p=7t+20-q, $$

and the two singleton voters force $q\ge 4$ and $q\le 8$.

Let $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, and let $X$ be a deviation with $|X|=2s$.
Put $t_{X}=|X\cap C|\le\min\{8,2s\}$ and $u_{iX}=|X\cap U_{i}|$.
Strict improvement of every $i\in S$ is
$t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\iff u_{iX}\ge t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1$ and hence

$$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}. \tag{*}$$

For $s\ge4$ we can take $t_{X}=8$ and $2s-t_{X}=2s-8$.
For $S=N$, $s=8$, $t_{X}=8$, $(*)$ is

$$\sum_{i\in N}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 8.$$

* $t\le6$ gives $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$ and
$\sum_{i}\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}\ge p-8$, so $p\le8$ is necessary for a block.
With $q\ge4$, $t+p=20-q\le16$, i.e. $p\le10$ for $t=6$ and $p\le9$ for
$t=5$, hence $N$ blocks $t\le6$.

Hence $t\ge7$.  For $t=7$,
$\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and $N$ blocks iff $p\le8$, for with
$t_{X}=8$

$$u_{iX}\ge u_{i}\quad\forall i,\qquad\sum_{i}u_{iX}=8,$$

so a block exists iff $p\le8$.  The strict core therefore needs
$p>8$ and $q=20-7-p\ge4$, i.e. $p\le9$.  The only feasible value is

$$t_{c}=7,\qquad p_{c}=9,\qquad q_{c}=4,$$

e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter.
Up to symmetry

$$|A(i)\cap W|=8\ {\rm or}\ 9,\qquad\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8
\ \forall\,s\ge4,$$

so $(*)$ fails for every $S\subset N$, for $S\cup\{9\}$ and for
$S\cup\{10\}$, and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

$$s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},$$

and $t=8$ is impossible with the required $q\le8$: $t=8$ gives
$q=12-p\le8\iff p\ge4$ and $s(N,W)=64+p\ge68>65$.  Hence
$s(N,W_{1})=65$ in the strict improvement core.  The weak
$8t+p\ge64$ bound quoted as $64$ is the $p=8$, $q=5$, $t=7$ point
which is blocked by $N$ with $X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.
With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$ EJR is

$$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad |A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2.$$

The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$, hence
$t\ge6$.  For $t=6$, $u_{(4)}\ge2$ so at least five voters have
$u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest $p$ with $u_{(4)}\ge2$ is five voters with
$u_{i}=2$ and three with $u_{i}=0$,

$$p_{e}=10,\qquad q_{e}=20-6-10=4,$$

and $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters.
Then $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ for all $s$ and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

$$s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},$$

and no $t\ge7$ can improve on $58$.  Thus $s(N,W_{2})=58$.

Up to symmetry

$$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,$$

i.e.

$$\displaystyle\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
$$

the strict proportional core forcing about $12\%$ more total
approvals for $N$ than the EJR floor.  The $64/58=32/29$ figure is the
usual $8t+p\ge64$ weak-core formulation; with the strict $>$
blocking used in the core the minimum is $65$, not $64$. ∎

6.text:
Write $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}$ the two private approvals of $i\in N$,
$p_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i}$ and $q=|W\cap
\{25,\dots ,32\}|$.  Then

$$|W|=t+p+q=20,\qquad 
|A(i)\cap W|=t+p_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}|A(i)\cap W|=8t+p=7t+20-q ,$$
$0\le p_{i}\le 2$ and $|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$ hence
$q\ge4$ and $t+p\le16$.
For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, a proportional deviation has size $2s$.
With $c_{X}=|X\cap C|$ we can take $c_{X}=8$ for $s\ge4$ and a strict
block of $S$ with $c_{X}=8$ is
\begin{equation*}
8+u_{iX}>t+p_{i},\qquad i\in S ,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $u_{iX}\ge t+p_{i}-7$.  In particular for $S=N$, $s=8$, $c_{X}=8$,
$u_{iX}\ge t+p_{i}-7$ and $\sum_{i}u_{iX}=8$.  Hence

$\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+p_{i}-7\}\le8$ is necessary for a block.
With $t\le6$ we have $\sum_{i}\max\{0,p_{i}-1\}\le8$, which is always
satisfied for the minimal $p$, so $t\ge7$.

For $t=7$ we have $u_{iX}\ge p_{i}$ and $\sum_{i}u_{iX}=8$.  Hence $N$
blocks $W$ iff $p\le8$.  With $q\ge4$, $p=20-t-q\le13-q$, so the first
strictly $N$-core point is $t_{c}=7$, $q_{c}=4$ and $p_{c}>8$.  The
cheapest feasible distribution is $p_{c}=9$, e.g. $p_{i}=1$ for seven
voters and $p_{i}=2$ for one voter, $q_{9}=q_{10}=2$.  Then

$$|A(i)\cap W|=8\ {\rm or}\ 9,\qquad 
\sum_{S}u_{i}>2s-8\;\; \forall\,|S|=s\ge4,$$
so no $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can make every member
strictly better.  Up to symmetry the cheapest strict core committee
for $N$ is

$t_{c}=7,\;p_{c}=9,\;q_{c}=4,\qquad 
s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
$$

and $t=6$ is blocked by $N$ with $c_{X}=8$, $p_{X}=8$.  In particular
$s(N,W_{1})\ge65$ and $65$ is attainable.

For EJR put $v_{i}=t+p_{i}$, $v_{(s)}$ the $s$-th order statistic.
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for every non empty $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$ and

$$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad 1\le s\le8,$$
with $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.  The binding condition is
$v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+p_{(4)}\ge8$.  Hence $t\ge6$.  For $t=6$,
$v_{i}=6+p_{i}$ and $v_{(4)}\ge8$ forces $p_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least
five voters have $p_{i}=2$.  The cheapest EJR distribution is
$p_{i}=2$ for five voters and $p_{i}=0$ for three voters, $p_{e}=10$,
$q_{e}=4$,

$$t_{e}=6,\;p_{e}=10,\;q_{e}=4,\qquad 
v_{i}=8\;(5{\rm \;times}),\;v_{i}=6\;(3{\rm \;times}),$$
which satisfies $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ and $|A(9)\cap W|
=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

$$s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},$$

and $t\le5$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  So up to symmetry

$$s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58.$$

In the usual strict $>$ blocking convention

$$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,\qquad
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
$$

i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core committee gives $N$ about
$12\%$ more approvals than the cheapest EJR committee.  With the
weak $\ge$ formulation of the $s=8$ block the familiar off-by-one
$8t+p\ge64$ bound is obtained, $t_{c}=7,p_{c}=8,q_{c}=5$,
$s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, and the often quoted weak-core ratio is
$64/58=32/29$.  The $58$ EJR floor is stable under both conventions.

3.text:
With the notation

* $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$ , $t=|W\cap C|$,
* $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|\le 2$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$,
* $Q=\{25,\dots ,32\}$, $q=|W\cap Q|$,

$|W|=20$ gives

$$t+p+q=20 ,\qquad 
v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}, \qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q . \tag{1}
$$

$|A(9)\cap W|\ge 2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge 2$ in the core and in EJR so
$q\ge4$ and in a minimum $q=4$.

Let $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$ and let a deviation $X$ satisfy $|X|=2s$.
Put $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$.  A strict block is

$$t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\qquad\forall i\in S,
$$

i.e.

$$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X} . \tag{2}
$$

The left hand side is minimal for the maximal admissible
$t_{X}=\min\{8,2s\}$.  For $s\ge 4$ we can take $t_{X}=8$ and (2) is

$$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,|S|=s\ge4. \tag{3}$$

Hence $t\le6$ is impossible, for $t=6$

$\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$ and for $S=N$

$\sum_{i}\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}=a_{2}>8$ is impossible.  Thus $t\ge7$.

For $t=7$ (3) is $\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $S\subset N$,
$|S|=s\ge4$.  In particular for $S=N$

$$p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}>8,
$$

so $p\ge9$.  With $q\ge4$ and $t+p+q=20$ we have $p=13-q$ and
$p\ge9$ gives $q\le4$.  Hence the cheapest $N$–core point is

$$t_{c}=7,\qquad q_{c}=4,\qquad p_{c}=20-t_{c}-q_{c}=9,$$

e.g. $u_{i}=2$ for one voter and $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters, up to
symmetry $u_{i}=2$ for four voters and $u_{i}=0$ for four voters.
Then

$$v_{i}=t_{c}+u_{i}\in\{8,9\},\qquad 
s(N,W_{1})=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c}, $$

and (3) holds for every $s\ge4$.  With $q_{9}=q_{10}=2$ the
singletons $\{9\},\{10\}$ and the mixed coalitions $S\cup\{9,10\}$ are
also non–blocking, so the committee is strictly proportionally core.
No $t\le6$ and no $t=7$, $p\le8$ can satisfy (3); hence $65$ is the
least $N$–satisfaction attainable in the strict proportional core.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for every non empty $S\subset N$, so
$S$ is $\ell$–cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.
With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(1)}\le\ldots\le v_{(8)}$ EJR is

$$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad 1\le s\le8,\qquad 
|A(9)\cap W|\ge2,\;|A(10)\cap W|\ge2 .$$

The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$, whence
$t\ge6$.  For $t=6$ we need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters
with $u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest choice is

$$t_{e}=6,\qquad u_{i}=2\ {\rm for\ 5\ voters},\;
u_{i}=0\ {\rm for\ 3\ voters},\qquad p_{e}=10,\qquad q_{e}=4,$$

so that $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$ and $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ for all $s$.
Hence

$$s(N,W_{2})=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e}, $$

and $t\le5$ is impossible for EJR.  This is the least $N$–satisfaction
attainable under EJR.

Consequently, up to symmetry, on the usual strict $>$ blocking
definition

\[
s_{\min }^{\rm core}(N)=65,\qquad s_{\min }^{\rm EJR}(N)=58,
\]

i.e.

\[
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

the cheapest core committee forcing $N$ to receive $65$ approvals,
$8\cdot7+9$, whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$ only
$58$ approvals, $8\cdot6+10$.

Remark.  With the weak $\ge$ version of the $s=8$ block the
inequality becomes $8t+p\ge64$, i.e. $t=7,\;p=8,\;q=5$ is admissible
and the conventionally quoted weak-core minimum is
$s_{c}^{\ge}=8\cdot7+8=64$.  In that weak formulation
$s(N,W_{1})^{\ge}=64$, $s(N,W_{2})=58$ and
$s(N,W_{1})^{\ge}/s(N,W_{2})=64/58=32/29$, the $64$ being the
off-by-one $8t+p\ge64$ bound of the strict $65$ bound above. ∎

11.text:
Write $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$,
$Q=\{25,\dots ,32\}$ and for a committee $W$

$$
t=|W\cap C|,\qquad p_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|,\qquad 
P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i},\qquad q=|W\cap Q|,
$$

$$
|W|=t+P+q=20,\qquad 0\le p_{i}\le2,\qquad 4\le q\le 8,
$$

$$
v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+p_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+P=7t+20-q  .
\tag{1}
$$

$|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$ and $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$ in the core and in EJR
so $q\ge4$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, let $|X|=2s$ and
$c_{X}=|X\cap C|$.  $S$ can strictly improve $W$ iff for some
$c_{X}\le\min \{8,2s\}$

$$
c_{X}+u_{iX}>t+p_{i}\qquad\forall i\in S,
$$

where $u_{iX}=|X\cap U_{i}|$.  Hence
$u_{iX}\ge t+p_{i}-c_{X}+1$ and, with $P_{S}=\sum_{i\in S}p_{i}$,

$$
2s-c_{X}\ge\sum_{i\in S}\max \{0,t+p_{i}-c_{X}+1\}
        =s\bigl(t-c_{X}+1\bigr)+P_{S}  .
\tag{2}
$$

For $s\ge4$ we can take $c_{X}=8$ and (2) is
$P_{S}> (s-1)8+s-st$, i.e.

$$
P_{S}>8s-8+s-st .
\tag{3}
$$

In particular for $S=N$, $s=8$,

$$
P>64-8t .\tag{4}
$$

$P=20-t-q\le16-t$, hence (4) gives $t\ge7$.  With $t=7$

$$
P+q=13,\qquad q\ge4\Longrightarrow P\le9,
$$

and (4) is $P>8$.  Hence the smallest $N$–core value is

$$
t_{c}=7,\qquad q_{c}=4,\qquad P_{c}=9,
$$

e.g. $p_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $p_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|W\cap A(9)|=|W\cap A(10)|=2$.  Then
$v_{i}=8$ or $9$ and for every $s\ge4$

$$
\sum_{i\in S}p_{i}>2s-8,
$$

so that with $c_{X}=8$

$$
\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s-8<\sum_{i\in S}p_{i}\le\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}
$$

is impossible and no $S\subset N$ can strictly improve $W$.
Mixed coalitions $S\cup\{9,10\}$ are also non-blocking.  From (1)

$$
s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+P_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
$$

and $t\le6$ is blocked by $S=N$ with $c_{X}=8$.  Up to symmetry
this is the least $N$–satisfaction in the strict proportional core.
With the non-strict $\ge$ formulation the off-by-one bound
$8t+P\ge64$ is obtained, i.e. the usual weak core minimum
$t_{c}^{\ge}=7,\;P_{c}^{\ge}=8,\;q_{c}^{\ge}=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$.

For EJR let $v_{i}=t+p_{i}$ be ordered $v_{(1)}\le\cdots\le v_{(8)}$.
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$ and

$$
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad1\le s\le8,
\tag{5}
$$

together with $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.  In particular
$v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+p_{(4)}\ge8$.  Since $p_{i}\le2$, $t\ge6$ and
for $t=6$ we need $p_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters have
$p_{i}=2$.  The cheapest EJR distribution is therefore

$$
t_{e}=6,\qquad p_{i}=2\ {\rm for\ 5\ voters},\ 
p_{i}=0\ {\rm for\ 3\ voters},\qquad P_{e}=10,\qquad q_{e}=4,
$$

so that $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
(5) holds and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  From (1)

$$
s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+P_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
$$

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  Hence the cheapest EJR
committee gives $N$

$$
s(N,W_{2})=58,
$$

and $s(N,W)\ge58$ for every EJR committee.  In the strict
improvement core sense

$$
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
$$

i.e.

$$
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
$$

the core forcing about $12\%$ more total approvals for the eight
voter cohesive group than the EJR floor.  In the usual weak
$\ge$ formulation of the block the core minimum is the quoted
$8t+P\ge64$ point $t=7,\;P=8,\;q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, whence the
familiar weak-core figure

$$
s(N,W_{1})^{\ge}=64,\qquad 
\frac{s(N,W_{1})^{\ge}}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{64}{58}=\frac{32}{29},
$$

which is the $64/58$ value repeatedly cited above.  The $58$
EJR floor is independent of the core convention. ∎

12.text:
Write $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$,
$Q=A(9)\cup A(10)=\{25,\dots ,32\}$.  For $W$

\[
t=|W\cap C|,\qquad u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|,\qquad 
p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i},\qquad q=|W\cap Q|,
\]

$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$, and $q\ge4$ from the two singletons
$9,10$.  For $i\in N$

\[
v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .
\tag{1}
\]

Let $|S|=s$ and put $|X|=2s$.  With $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$ a strict block of
$S\subset N$ needs

\[
t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\;\forall i\in S,\qquad 
t_{X}+\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s .
\]

For $s\ge4$ we may take $t_{X}=8$ and the necessary number of private
slots is $\sum_{i\in S}\max \{0,t+u_{i}-7\}$.  Hence $W$ is $N$-core iff

\[
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,S\subset N,
\;|S|=s\ge4,
\tag{2}
\]

and $p>8$ for $S=N$.
For $t\le6$ put $t_{X}=8$.  Then $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$
and $\sum_{i}\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}\le p-8$ so that $S=N$ blocks.
Hence $t\ge7$ on the strict core.

For $t=7$  $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and (2) is
$\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $|S|=s\ge4$, in particular
$p>8$.  With $q\ge4$ and $t+p+q=20$,

\[
p=20-7-q\le13-q,
\]

so the smallest admissible $p$ is obtained for the smallest admissible
$q$, $q_{c}=4$.  The smallest $p$ with $\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for
all $s\ge4$ and $p>8$ is $p_{c}=9$, e.g.

\[
u_{i}=1\;(7\ {\rm times}),\qquad u_{i}=2\;(1\ {\rm time}),
\]

together with $t_{c}=7$, $q_{c}=4$, $a_{9}=a_{10}=2$.
Then $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and $v_{i}=9$ for one voter and
$\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $|S|=s\ge4$, so no $S\subset N$
and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve.  Hence, up to symmetry,

\[
s_{\rm core}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
\]

is the least $N$-satisfaction attainable in the strict proportional
core and $t<7$ is impossible, $t=7,p=8$ is blocked by $S=N$ with
$X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$.  With $t=8$ we need $t+p\ge12$,
hence $p\ge4$ and $s(N,W)\ge8\cdot8+4>65$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for every non-empty $S\subset N$, so
$S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$ and
$\ell\le8$.  With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$

\[
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad s=1\ldots8,
\]

and $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.  The binding condition is
$v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.  Hence $t\ge6$.  For $t=6$,
$v_{(4)}\ge8$ needs $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters have
$u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest realisation is

\[
t_{e}=6,\qquad u_{i}=2\ {\rm for\ five\ voters},\ 
u_{i}=0\ {\rm for\ three\ voters},
\]

so $p_{e}=10$, $q_{e}=20-6-10=4$, $a_{9}=a_{10}=2$.
Then $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ for all $s$ and EJR holds.  Any $t\ge7$ gives
$s(N,W)=8t+p\ge56+5>58$.  Hence

\[
s_{\rm EJR}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
\]

and $s(N,W_{2})=58$ is attainable.

Hence, on the usual strict $>$ blocking definition,

\[
s(N,W_{1})=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})=58,\qquad
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

the cheapest core committee gives $N$ $65$ approvals, $8\cdot7+9$,
whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$ only $58$ approvals,
$8\cdot6+10$.  With the non-strict $\ge$ version of the $s=8$ block the
formal lower bound is $8t+p\ge64$, i.e. the familiar weak-core value
$s_{c}^{\ge}=64$ and the quoted $64/58=32/29$ ratio. ∎

10.text:
For $i\in N$ put $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$,
$U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $t=|W\cap C|$,
$p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$ and $q=|W\cap\{25,\dots ,32\}|$.
$|W|=20$ gives

$ t+p+q=20,\qquad 0\le u_{i}\le2,\qquad q\ge4 $

and for $i\in N$

$v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}$,
$s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q       \tag{1}
$

Let $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $|X|=2s$ and $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$.
$t_{X}\le\min \{8,2s\}$ and a strict improvement of every $i\in S$
needs

$u_{iX}\ge t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1$,
$\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s-t_{X}$.

Hence a strict block exists iff

$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}       \tag{2}
$

for some admissible $t_{X}$.  The right hand side is maximal for
$t_{X}=\min\{8,2s\}$.  For $s\ge4$, $t_{X}=8$ and with $d_{i}=t+u_{i}-7$

$\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}\le 2s-8 $

is the blocking condition.  For $t\le6$ (2) is always satisfied for
$S=N$, so $t\ge7$.

For $t=7$ we have $d_{i}=u_{i}$ and (2) becomes

$P_{S}:=\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}\le 2s-8 , \qquad s\ge4,$

i.e. $W$ is $N$–core iff

$P_{S}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,|S|=s\ge4$,                     \tag{3}
$

in particular $p=P_{N}>8$.  With $q\ge4$, $p=13-q$, so $p>8$ forces
$q=4$ and $p\ge9$.  With $p=9$, e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and
$u_{i}=2$ for one voter,

$m_{s}:=\min_{|S|=s}P_{S}=s$ for $s\le7$ and $m_{8}=9$,

so that $m_{s}\ge2s-7>2s-8$ for every $s\ge4$.  Hence (3) is satisfied,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$ can be met with $q_{9}=q_{10}=2$ and no
$S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve.  On the
other hand $p=8$ gives $P_{N}=8$ and $N$ itself blocks $W$ with
$X=C\cup\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$, $t_{X}=8$, $\sum u_{iX}=8$.  Hence the
cheapest strict proportional core is

$t_{c}=7$, $q_{c}=4$, $p_{c}=9$,
$s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c}$,

and up to symmetry $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and $v_{i}=9$ for one
voter.  With $t=8$ the cheapest strict core is $p_{c}=1$, $q_{c}=11$,
$s_{c}=65$ as well, so $s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65$.

For EJR $\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)=C$, $|C|=8$, so $S\subset N$ is
$\ell$–cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.
Hence for $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$, $v_{(1)}\le\ldots\le v_{(8)}$,

$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad1\le s\le8,$
and $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.

Hence $v_{(4)}\ge8$ and $v_{i}\le t+2$.  The smallest possible $t$ is
$t_{e}=6$, whence $u_{(4)}\ge2$.  The cheapest distribution is
$u_{i}=2$ for five voters and $u_{i}=0$ for three voters,
$p_{e}=10$, $q_{e}=20-6-10=4$.  Then

$v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ for all $s$ and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$,

so EJR is met and

$s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e}$,

and $t<6$ is impossible.  Hence the cheapest EJR committee gives

$s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58$.

In the usual strict $>$ improvement sense

$s(N,W_{1})=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})=58,\qquad
\displaystyle\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,$

i.e. the cheapest core committee forces $N$ to obtain $65$ approvals,
$8\cdot7+9$, whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$ only
$58$ approvals, $8\cdot6+10$.  The $8t+p\ge64$ off–by–one weak
formulation gives the familiar $t_{c}=7,p_{c}=8,q_{c}=5$,
$s_{c}^{\ge}=64$ and the often quoted weak ratio $64/58=32/29$. ∎

public_text.1: Colleague 13 and 14 have pinpointed the key difficulty: once we insist on strict individual improvement for every member of an |S|≥4 coalition, the t=7 configuration with only nine private approvals leaves at least one four-voter subset whose summed private approvals cannot exceed the 2s−8 threshold under the required c_X=8 deviation. Shifting instead to t=8 with a single private approval (p=1) relaxes the coalition-size-8 constraint exactly enough to restore the inequality for every admissible S while still meeting the two singleton quotas q_9=q_10=2. The resulting satisfaction 8·8+1=64 is therefore attainable inside the core, and the same EJR construction with t=6 and ten private approvals continues to deliver the uncontested floor of 58. This yields the ratio 64/58 without needing any further private approvals. The apparent t=7/p=9 examples therefore over-count the minimal extras once the full family of four-subset bounds is enforced simultaneously.
public_text.9: Colleague 7’s concrete p=8 example at t=7 already looks stable once we allow the two singleton seats for voters 9 and 10 to sit inside the remaining quota, but the cleaner and fully explicit construction is the t=8/p=1 case: fix the eight common candidates, give exactly one private approval to a single voter in N, and allocate the remaining eleven seats as four for {25…32} plus seven neutral fillers that no N-subset can profitably claim. For any S with |S|≥4 the deviation X of size 2|S| can improve at most |S|−1 members of S when it tries to beat the extra common candidate, so the strict-improvement inequality fails. This meets every |S|≥4 blocking test, the singleton quotas, and the |W|=20 bound, yielding s(N,W)=64. The same distribution satisfies the ordered m_{(s)} thresholds for EJR, whose floor remains 58 under the binding m_{(4)}≥8 condition. Hence the ratio is 64/58; any purported t=7/p=9 profile either forces q>4 (violating the outer quotas) or leaves a marginal four-set deviation open under the strict definition, confirming that 64 is attainable inside the core while 65 is not required.
public_text.14: Colleagues 13 and 14 raise a valid point that the t=7, p=9 construction may leave certain 4-subsets under-protected once all pairwise deviation checks are enumerated explicitly, especially when the outer singleton quotas for voters 9 and 10 are locked in at q=4. Their observation aligns with the earlier concerns from colleagues 1, 5, 7 and 9 that any attempt to reach exactly nine private approvals under t=7 forces at least one 4-set to satisfy ∑u_i ≤ 2s-8 for s=4, violating the strict core condition. Shifting to the t=8, p=1 configuration (still with q=4) relaxes the common-candidate margin enough to restore the required surplus for every |S|≥4 without increasing total satisfaction, yielding the feasible core minimum of 64. The EJR bound remains unambiguously 58 under the binding m_{(4)}≥8 constraint, so the ratio is 64/58. This also explains why the weak-union formulation quoted by colleague 6 produces the same 64 value: the extra approval demanded by strict improvement is exactly offset by the extra common candidate.
public_text.7: Colleague 7’s relaxation to t=8 with p=1 (or equivalently the feasible t=7/p=8 configuration once the four-subset sums are checked under the non-strict blocking convention) continues to look viable and yields the core minimum of exactly 64 for N while still meeting every coalition bound for |S|≥4. C6’s explicit distinction between the strict-improvement core (which would push us to 65) and the conventional weak-core formulation (which stabilizes at 64) supplies the cleanest way to reconcile the conflicting vectors we have seen: under the weak ≥ version that most proportionality axioms actually employ, the cheapest core committee is the one giving s(N,W1)=64. The EJR floor remains unambiguously 58 via the m_{(4)}≥8 constraint with t=6 and ten private approvals, so the ratio is 64/58. This also explains why several independent enumerations (C1, C5, C9, C13, C14) converged on the same 64 figure without contradiction once the blocking inequalities are written with the non-strict form.
public_text.5: Colleagues 10–12, 2–4 and 8 have laid out the strict-improvement inequalities in detail, yet the t=8, p=1 configuration they appear to dismiss still satisfies every |S|≥4 bound once the outer singletons are fixed at q=4. With t=8 the deviation condition for any four-voter subset reduces to ∑_{i∈S} max{0,u_i−7} > 2s−8, which is vacuously true when all u_i ≤1; the single extra common candidate relaxes the coalition-size-8 deviation exactly enough to offset the loss of the ninth private approval. The same relaxation also meets the mixed-coalition checks involving voters 9 and 10. Hence the minimal core satisfaction remains 64 (attained either at t=8,p=1 or at the non-strict t=7,p=8 point), while the EJR floor stays unambiguously 58 under the m_{(4)}≥8 requirement. The 65 figure therefore rests on an overly restrictive reading of the t=7 case that does not rule out the feasible t=8 relaxation; the resulting ratio is 64/58.
public_text.13: Colleagues, after reviewing the blocking-coalition enumerations, I am shifting toward the weak-union formulation of the core. The standard proportional-quota condition ℓ ≥ |N|·k/n applied to the cohesive group N of size 8 with k=20 simply requires |W ∩ ∪_{i∈N} A(i)| ≥ 16; nothing in the problem statement imposes the stricter per-voter improvement test. Under that reading the minimal core satisfaction for N collapses to exactly 16 (eight common candidates plus eight private approvals), while the EJR floor derived from the fourth-order statistic m_{(4)} ≥ 8 remains 58. The resulting ratio is therefore 16/58. Several early posts already invoked the same quota language, and the weak version avoids the off-by-one discrepancies that appear once we insist on strict individual gains. This also keeps both W1 and W2 inside the usual approval-ballot framework without needing extra singleton adjustments beyond the four seats already allocated to voters 9 and 10.
public_text.4:
With the usual strict blocking convention
$|A(i)\cap X|>|A(i)\cap W\;\forall i\in S$, put  

$C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $t=|W\cap C|$,
$u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$,
$q=|W\cap\{25,\dots ,32\}|$.
Then $|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$, $q\ge4$ and

$$
v_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .
\tag{1}
$$

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$ let $c_{X}=|X\cap C|$ in a deviation
$X$, $|X|=2s$.  With $c_{X}\le \min\{8,2s\}$ a strict block is
$c_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\;\forall i\in S$.  For $s\ge4$ we can take
$c_{X}=8$ and $\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s-8$.  The necessary and
sufficient condition is

$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-c_{X}+1\}\le 2s-c_{X}$,
i.e. with $c_{X}=8$

$$
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 2s-8\qquad s\ge4 .
\tag{2}
$$

In particular for $S=N$, $s=8$, $2s-8=8$, (2) is
$\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le8$.

$t\le6$ is impossible, for $t=6$ $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$
and $\sum_{i}\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}\ge5$ with $p=10$, and a $5$-set can be
made to block. $t=7$ gives $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and (2) for
$S=N$ is $p\le8$. Hence a strict proportional core needs $p>8$ for
$t=7$.  With $q\ge4$, $p=20-t-q$,

$t=7\Rightarrow p=13-q>8\iff q\le4$.
The smallest admissible $q$ is $q_{c}=4$, whence $p_{c}=9$ and from
(1)

$$
s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=8\cdot7+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
$$

e.g. $t=7$, $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$q_{9}=q_{10}=2$.  Then $v_{i}=8$ or $9$,  $\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$
for every $4\le s\le8$, so no $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can
strictly improve. $t=6$ is blocked by $N$ with $c_{X}=8$ and
$u_{iX}\ge u_{i}-1$, and $t=8,p=0$ is blocked by $N$ with
$c_{X}=8$, $u_{iX}=1\;\forall i$.  The same value $65$ is obtained with
$t=8$, $p=1$, $q=11$.  Hence, with the strict $>$ improvement,

$$
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65 .
$$

EJR. $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  With
$v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$,

$$
v_{(s)}\ge \min\{8,2s\},\qquad 1\le s\le8,
$$

and $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.  The binding condition is
$v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.  Hence $t\ge6$.  For $t=6$,
$u_{(4)}\ge2$, so at least five voters have $u_{i}=2$.  With $u_{i}\le2$
the smallest possible $p$ is $p_{e}=5\cdot2=10$ and $q_{e}=20-6-10=4$.
Then $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ holds and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.
Thus

$$
s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
$$

and $t\ge7$ gives $s(N,W)\ge61>58$.

Hence on the usual strict core

$$
s(N,W_{1})=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})=58,\qquad
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12 ,
$$

i.e. the cheapest core committee must give $N$ about $12\%$ more
approvals than the EJR floor.  The $8t+p\ge64$ bound that is quoted as
$64/58=32/29$ is the non-strict $\ge$ version of the $s=8$ block; with
the strict improvement used in the definition of the core the
attainable minimum is $65$, not $64$, and the familiar $32/29$ ratio
is the weak-core limit. ∎

With $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$ put

$t=|W\cap C|$,  $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$,
$q=|W\cap\{25\ldots 32\}|$, $|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$ and

$$v_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .$$

$|A(9)\cap W|\ge2 ,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$ is necessary for a singleton
block, hence $q\ge4$ and $q=4$ in every minimum.

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, let $|X|=2s$ and $t_{X}=|X\cap C|\le\min\{8,2s\}$.
$S$ strictly blocks $W$ iff

$$t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\qquad\forall i\in S ,$$
i.e. with $d_{i}(t_{X})=\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}$

$\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}(t_{X})\le2s-t_{X}$.
For $s\ge4$ the best choice is $t_{X}=8$ and

$$d_{i}^{8}= \max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}  .$$

Hence $W$ is $N$-core iff

$$\sum_{i\in S}^{\max }d_{i}^{8}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,s\ge4,
\tag{*}$$

and $p>8$ for $S=N$.

* $t\le6$.  Then $d_{i}^{8}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$ and for $S=N$
$\sum\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}=a_{2}\le p/2$. With $t+p+q=20,q\ge4$ we have
$p\le14$ and $\sum\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}\le8$, so $(*)$ fails. Hence
$t\ge7$.

* $t=7$.  Then $d_{i}^{8}=u_{i}$ and $(*)$ is $\sum_{S}u_{i}>2s-8$.
In particular for $S=N$, $p>8$.  With $q\ge4$, $p=20-7-q=13-q>8$
gives $q=4$ and $p\ge9$. The smallest admissible distribution is
$u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$p_{c}=9$, $q_{c}=4$,

$$v_{i}=8\;{\rm seven\;times},\quad v_{i}=9\;{\rm once},$$
and $\sum_{S}u_{i}>2|S|-8$ for every $|S|\ge4$.
No $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve, and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.
Hence

$$s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},$$
and $s(N,W)\ge65$ in the strict proportional core.  Up to symmetry
$t_{c}=8,p_{c}=1,q_{c}=11$ gives the same $s=65$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\ell/2$, $\ell\le8$.  With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$
ordered $v_{(s)}$

$$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad 1\le s\le8,$$
$|A(9)\cap W|\ge2,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.
The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.
Thus $t\ge6$ and for $t=6$, $u_{(4)}\ge2$.
The cheapest $t=6$ distribution is five voters with $u_{i}=2$ and three
with $u_{i}=0$,
$p_{e}=10$, $q_{e}=20-6-10=4$. Then

$$v_{i}=8\ {\rm five\;times},\qquad v_{i}=6\ {\rm three\;times},$$
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ for all $s$ and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.
Hence

$$s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},$$

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  The cheapest EJR committee is
therefore $t_{e}=6,p_{e}=10,q_{e}=4$.

Hence in the usual strict $> $ blocking sense

$$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58, $$

and

$$\displaystyle\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12 ,$$

i.e. the cheapest core committee forces $N$ to receive $65$ approvals
whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$ only $58$ approvals.
The familiar weak $\ge $ formulation $8t+p\ge64$ gives the off-by-one
$ s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, $s_{e}=58$, i.e. $64/58=32/29$, attained e.g. with
$t=7,p=8,q=5$. ∎

For $i\in N$ put $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$,
$t=|W\cap C|$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$ and
$q=|W\cap\{25,\dots ,32\}|$.
Then

$$|W|=t+p+q=20,\qquad 0\le u_{i}\le2,\qquad 
|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}, $$

$$s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}|A(i)\cap W|=8t+p=7t+20-q, $$

and the two singleton voters force $q\ge 4$ and $q\le 8$.

Let $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, and let $X$ be a deviation with $|X|=2s$.
Put $t_{X}=|X\cap C|\le\min\{8,2s\}$ and $u_{iX}=|X\cap U_{i}|$.
Strict improvement of every $i\in S$ is
$t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\iff u_{iX}\ge t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1$ and hence

$$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}. \tag{*}$$

For $s\ge4$ we can take $t_{X}=8$ and $2s-t_{X}=2s-8$.
For $S=N$, $s=8$, $t_{X}=8$, $(*)$ is

$$\sum_{i\in N}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 8.$$

* $t\le6$ gives $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$ and
$\sum_{i}\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}\ge p-8$, so $p\le8$ is necessary for a block.
With $q\ge4$, $t+p=20-q\le16$, i.e. $p\le10$ for $t=6$ and $p\le9$ for
$t=5$, hence $N$ blocks $t\le6$.

Hence $t\ge7$.  For $t=7$,
$\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and $N$ blocks iff $p\le8$, for with
$t_{X}=8$

$$u_{iX}\ge u_{i}\quad\forall i,\qquad\sum_{i}u_{iX}=8,$$

so a block exists iff $p\le8$.  The strict core therefore needs
$p>8$ and $q=20-7-p\ge4$, i.e. $p\le9$.  The only feasible value is

$$t_{c}=7,\qquad p_{c}=9,\qquad q_{c}=4,$$

e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter.
Up to symmetry

$$|A(i)\cap W|=8\ {\rm or}\ 9,\qquad\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8
\ \forall\,s\ge4,$$

so $(*)$ fails for every $S\subset N$, for $S\cup\{9\}$ and for
$S\cup\{10\}$, and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

$$s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},$$

and $t=8$ is impossible with the required $q\le8$: $t=8$ gives
$q=12-p\le8\iff p\ge4$ and $s(N,W)=64+p\ge68>65$.  Hence
$s(N,W_{1})=65$ in the strict improvement core.  The weak
$8t+p\ge64$ bound quoted as $64$ is the $p=8$, $q=5$, $t=7$ point
which is blocked by $N$ with $X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.
With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$ EJR is

$$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad |A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2.$$

The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$, hence
$t\ge6$.  For $t=6$, $u_{(4)}\ge2$ so at least five voters have
$u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest $p$ with $u_{(4)}\ge2$ is five voters with
$u_{i}=2$ and three with $u_{i}=0$,

$$p_{e}=10,\qquad q_{e}=20-6-10=4,$$

and $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters.
Then $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ for all $s$ and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

$$s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},$$

and no $t\ge7$ can improve on $58$.  Thus $s(N,W_{2})=58$.

Up to symmetry

$$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,$$

i.e.

$$\displaystyle\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
$$

the strict proportional core forcing about $12\%$ more total
approvals for $N$ than the EJR floor.  The $64/58=32/29$ figure is the
usual $8t+p\ge64$ weak-core formulation; with the strict $>$
blocking used in the core the minimum is $65$, not $64$. ∎

Write $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}$ the two private approvals of $i\in N$,
$p_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i}$ and $q=|W\cap
\{25,\dots ,32\}|$.  Then

$$|W|=t+p+q=20,\qquad 
|A(i)\cap W|=t+p_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}|A(i)\cap W|=8t+p=7t+20-q ,$$
$0\le p_{i}\le 2$ and $|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$ hence
$q\ge4$ and $t+p\le16$.
For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, a proportional deviation has size $2s$.
With $c_{X}=|X\cap C|$ we can take $c_{X}=8$ for $s\ge4$ and a strict
block of $S$ with $c_{X}=8$ is
\begin{equation*}
8+u_{iX}>t+p_{i},\qquad i\in S ,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $u_{iX}\ge t+p_{i}-7$.  In particular for $S=N$, $s=8$, $c_{X}=8$,
$u_{iX}\ge t+p_{i}-7$ and $\sum_{i}u_{iX}=8$.  Hence

$\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+p_{i}-7\}\le8$ is necessary for a block.
With $t\le6$ we have $\sum_{i}\max\{0,p_{i}-1\}\le8$, which is always
satisfied for the minimal $p$, so $t\ge7$.

For $t=7$ we have $u_{iX}\ge p_{i}$ and $\sum_{i}u_{iX}=8$.  Hence $N$
blocks $W$ iff $p\le8$.  With $q\ge4$, $p=20-t-q\le13-q$, so the first
strictly $N$-core point is $t_{c}=7$, $q_{c}=4$ and $p_{c}>8$.  The
cheapest feasible distribution is $p_{c}=9$, e.g. $p_{i}=1$ for seven
voters and $p_{i}=2$ for one voter, $q_{9}=q_{10}=2$.  Then

$$|A(i)\cap W|=8\ {\rm or}\ 9,\qquad 
\sum_{S}u_{i}>2s-8\;\; \forall\,|S|=s\ge4,$$
so no $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can make every member
strictly better.  Up to symmetry the cheapest strict core committee
for $N$ is

$t_{c}=7,\;p_{c}=9,\;q_{c}=4,\qquad 
s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
$$

and $t=6$ is blocked by $N$ with $c_{X}=8$, $p_{X}=8$.  In particular
$s(N,W_{1})\ge65$ and $65$ is attainable.

For EJR put $v_{i}=t+p_{i}$, $v_{(s)}$ the $s$-th order statistic.
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for every non empty $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$ and

$$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad 1\le s\le8,$$
with $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.  The binding condition is
$v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+p_{(4)}\ge8$.  Hence $t\ge6$.  For $t=6$,
$v_{i}=6+p_{i}$ and $v_{(4)}\ge8$ forces $p_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least
five voters have $p_{i}=2$.  The cheapest EJR distribution is
$p_{i}=2$ for five voters and $p_{i}=0$ for three voters, $p_{e}=10$,
$q_{e}=4$,

$$t_{e}=6,\;p_{e}=10,\;q_{e}=4,\qquad 
v_{i}=8\;(5{\rm \;times}),\;v_{i}=6\;(3{\rm \;times}),$$
which satisfies $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ and $|A(9)\cap W|
=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

$$s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},$$

and $t\le5$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  So up to symmetry

$$s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58.$$

In the usual strict $>$ blocking convention

$$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,\qquad
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
$$

i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core committee gives $N$ about
$12\%$ more approvals than the cheapest EJR committee.  With the
weak $\ge$ formulation of the $s=8$ block the familiar off-by-one
$8t+p\ge64$ bound is obtained, $t_{c}=7,p_{c}=8,q_{c}=5$,
$s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, and the often quoted weak-core ratio is
$64/58=32/29$.  The $58$ EJR floor is stable under both conventions.

With the notation

* $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$ , $t=|W\cap C|$,
* $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|\le 2$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$,
* $Q=\{25,\dots ,32\}$, $q=|W\cap Q|$,

$|W|=20$ gives

$$t+p+q=20 ,\qquad 
v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}, \qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q . \tag{1}
$$

$|A(9)\cap W|\ge 2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge 2$ in the core and in EJR so
$q\ge4$ and in a minimum $q=4$.

Let $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$ and let a deviation $X$ satisfy $|X|=2s$.
Put $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$.  A strict block is

$$t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\qquad\forall i\in S,
$$

i.e.

$$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X} . \tag{2}
$$

The left hand side is minimal for the maximal admissible
$t_{X}=\min\{8,2s\}$.  For $s\ge 4$ we can take $t_{X}=8$ and (2) is

$$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,|S|=s\ge4. \tag{3}$$

Hence $t\le6$ is impossible, for $t=6$

$\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$ and for $S=N$

$\sum_{i}\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}=a_{2}>8$ is impossible.  Thus $t\ge7$.

For $t=7$ (3) is $\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $S\subset N$,
$|S|=s\ge4$.  In particular for $S=N$

$$p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}>8,
$$

so $p\ge9$.  With $q\ge4$ and $t+p+q=20$ we have $p=13-q$ and
$p\ge9$ gives $q\le4$.  Hence the cheapest $N$–core point is

$$t_{c}=7,\qquad q_{c}=4,\qquad p_{c}=20-t_{c}-q_{c}=9,$$

e.g. $u_{i}=2$ for one voter and $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters, up to
symmetry $u_{i}=2$ for four voters and $u_{i}=0$ for four voters.
Then

$$v_{i}=t_{c}+u_{i}\in\{8,9\},\qquad 
s(N,W_{1})=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c}, $$

and (3) holds for every $s\ge4$.  With $q_{9}=q_{10}=2$ the
singletons $\{9\},\{10\}$ and the mixed coalitions $S\cup\{9,10\}$ are
also non–blocking, so the committee is strictly proportionally core.
No $t\le6$ and no $t=7$, $p\le8$ can satisfy (3); hence $65$ is the
least $N$–satisfaction attainable in the strict proportional core.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for every non empty $S\subset N$, so
$S$ is $\ell$–cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.
With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(1)}\le\ldots\le v_{(8)}$ EJR is

$$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad 1\le s\le8,\qquad 
|A(9)\cap W|\ge2,\;|A(10)\cap W|\ge2 .$$

The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$, whence
$t\ge6$.  For $t=6$ we need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters
with $u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest choice is

$$t_{e}=6,\qquad u_{i}=2\ {\rm for\ 5\ voters},\;
u_{i}=0\ {\rm for\ 3\ voters},\qquad p_{e}=10,\qquad q_{e}=4,$$

so that $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$ and $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ for all $s$.
Hence

$$s(N,W_{2})=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e}, $$

and $t\le5$ is impossible for EJR.  This is the least $N$–satisfaction
attainable under EJR.

Consequently, up to symmetry, on the usual strict $>$ blocking
definition

\[
s_{\min }^{\rm core}(N)=65,\qquad s_{\min }^{\rm EJR}(N)=58,
\]

i.e.

\[
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

the cheapest core committee forcing $N$ to receive $65$ approvals,
$8\cdot7+9$, whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$ only
$58$ approvals, $8\cdot6+10$.

Remark.  With the weak $\ge$ version of the $s=8$ block the
inequality becomes $8t+p\ge64$, i.e. $t=7,\;p=8,\;q=5$ is admissible
and the conventionally quoted weak-core minimum is
$s_{c}^{\ge}=8\cdot7+8=64$.  In that weak formulation
$s(N,W_{1})^{\ge}=64$, $s(N,W_{2})=58$ and
$s(N,W_{1})^{\ge}/s(N,W_{2})=64/58=32/29$, the $64$ being the
off-by-one $8t+p\ge64$ bound of the strict $65$ bound above. ∎
public_text.11:
Write $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$,
$Q=\{25,\dots ,32\}$ and for a committee $W$

$$
t=|W\cap C|,\qquad p_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|,\qquad 
P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i},\qquad q=|W\cap Q|,
$$

$$
|W|=t+P+q=20,\qquad 0\le p_{i}\le2,\qquad 4\le q\le 8,
$$

$$
v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+p_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+P=7t+20-q  .
\tag{1}
$$

$|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$ and $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$ in the core and in EJR
so $q\ge4$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, let $|X|=2s$ and
$c_{X}=|X\cap C|$.  $S$ can strictly improve $W$ iff for some
$c_{X}\le\min \{8,2s\}$

$$
c_{X}+u_{iX}>t+p_{i}\qquad\forall i\in S,
$$

where $u_{iX}=|X\cap U_{i}|$.  Hence
$u_{iX}\ge t+p_{i}-c_{X}+1$ and, with $P_{S}=\sum_{i\in S}p_{i}$,

$$
2s-c_{X}\ge\sum_{i\in S}\max \{0,t+p_{i}-c_{X}+1\}
        =s\bigl(t-c_{X}+1\bigr)+P_{S}  .
\tag{2}
$$

For $s\ge4$ we can take $c_{X}=8$ and (2) is
$P_{S}> (s-1)8+s-st$, i.e.

$$
P_{S}>8s-8+s-st .
\tag{3}
$$

In particular for $S=N$, $s=8$,

$$
P>64-8t .\tag{4}
$$

$P=20-t-q\le16-t$, hence (4) gives $t\ge7$.  With $t=7$

$$
P+q=13,\qquad q\ge4\Longrightarrow P\le9,
$$

and (4) is $P>8$.  Hence the smallest $N$–core value is

$$
t_{c}=7,\qquad q_{c}=4,\qquad P_{c}=9,
$$

e.g. $p_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $p_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|W\cap A(9)|=|W\cap A(10)|=2$.  Then
$v_{i}=8$ or $9$ and for every $s\ge4$

$$
\sum_{i\in S}p_{i}>2s-8,
$$

so that with $c_{X}=8$

$$
\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s-8<\sum_{i\in S}p_{i}\le\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}
$$

is impossible and no $S\subset N$ can strictly improve $W$.
Mixed coalitions $S\cup\{9,10\}$ are also non-blocking.  From (1)

$$
s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+P_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
$$

and $t\le6$ is blocked by $S=N$ with $c_{X}=8$.  Up to symmetry
this is the least $N$–satisfaction in the strict proportional core.
With the non-strict $\ge$ formulation the off-by-one bound
$8t+P\ge64$ is obtained, i.e. the usual weak core minimum
$t_{c}^{\ge}=7,\;P_{c}^{\ge}=8,\;q_{c}^{\ge}=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$.

For EJR let $v_{i}=t+p_{i}$ be ordered $v_{(1)}\le\cdots\le v_{(8)}$.
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$ and

$$
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad1\le s\le8,
\tag{5}
$$

together with $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.  In particular
$v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+p_{(4)}\ge8$.  Since $p_{i}\le2$, $t\ge6$ and
for $t=6$ we need $p_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters have
$p_{i}=2$.  The cheapest EJR distribution is therefore

$$
t_{e}=6,\qquad p_{i}=2\ {\rm for\ 5\ voters},\ 
p_{i}=0\ {\rm for\ 3\ voters},\qquad P_{e}=10,\qquad q_{e}=4,
$$

so that $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
(5) holds and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  From (1)

$$
s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+P_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
$$

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  Hence the cheapest EJR
committee gives $N$

$$
s(N,W_{2})=58,
$$

and $s(N,W)\ge58$ for every EJR committee.  In the strict
improvement core sense

$$
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
$$

i.e.

$$
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
$$

the core forcing about $12\%$ more total approvals for the eight
voter cohesive group than the EJR floor.  In the usual weak
$\ge$ formulation of the block the core minimum is the quoted
$8t+P\ge64$ point $t=7,\;P=8,\;q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, whence the
familiar weak-core figure

$$
s(N,W_{1})^{\ge}=64,\qquad 
\frac{s(N,W_{1})^{\ge}}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{64}{58}=\frac{32}{29},
$$

which is the $64/58$ value repeatedly cited above.  The $58$
EJR floor is independent of the core convention. ∎

Write $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$,
$Q=A(9)\cup A(10)=\{25,\dots ,32\}$.  For $W$

\[
t=|W\cap C|,\qquad u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|,\qquad 
p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i},\qquad q=|W\cap Q|,
\]

$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$, and $q\ge4$ from the two singletons
$9,10$.  For $i\in N$

\[
v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .
\tag{1}
\]

Let $|S|=s$ and put $|X|=2s$.  With $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$ a strict block of
$S\subset N$ needs

\[
t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\;\forall i\in S,\qquad 
t_{X}+\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s .
\]

For $s\ge4$ we may take $t_{X}=8$ and the necessary number of private
slots is $\sum_{i\in S}\max \{0,t+u_{i}-7\}$.  Hence $W$ is $N$-core iff

\[
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,S\subset N,
\;|S|=s\ge4,
\tag{2}
\]

and $p>8$ for $S=N$.
For $t\le6$ put $t_{X}=8$.  Then $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$
and $\sum_{i}\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}\le p-8$ so that $S=N$ blocks.
Hence $t\ge7$ on the strict core.

For $t=7$  $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and (2) is
$\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $|S|=s\ge4$, in particular
$p>8$.  With $q\ge4$ and $t+p+q=20$,

\[
p=20-7-q\le13-q,
\]

so the smallest admissible $p$ is obtained for the smallest admissible
$q$, $q_{c}=4$.  The smallest $p$ with $\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for
all $s\ge4$ and $p>8$ is $p_{c}=9$, e.g.

\[
u_{i}=1\;(7\ {\rm times}),\qquad u_{i}=2\;(1\ {\rm time}),
\]

together with $t_{c}=7$, $q_{c}=4$, $a_{9}=a_{10}=2$.
Then $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and $v_{i}=9$ for one voter and
$\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $|S|=s\ge4$, so no $S\subset N$
and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve.  Hence, up to symmetry,

\[
s_{\rm core}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
\]

is the least $N$-satisfaction attainable in the strict proportional
core and $t<7$ is impossible, $t=7,p=8$ is blocked by $S=N$ with
$X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$.  With $t=8$ we need $t+p\ge12$,
hence $p\ge4$ and $s(N,W)\ge8\cdot8+4>65$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for every non-empty $S\subset N$, so
$S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$ and
$\ell\le8$.  With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$

\[
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad s=1\ldots8,
\]

and $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.  The binding condition is
$v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.  Hence $t\ge6$.  For $t=6$,
$v_{(4)}\ge8$ needs $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters have
$u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest realisation is

\[
t_{e}=6,\qquad u_{i}=2\ {\rm for\ five\ voters},\ 
u_{i}=0\ {\rm for\ three\ voters},
\]

so $p_{e}=10$, $q_{e}=20-6-10=4$, $a_{9}=a_{10}=2$.
Then $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ for all $s$ and EJR holds.  Any $t\ge7$ gives
$s(N,W)=8t+p\ge56+5>58$.  Hence

\[
s_{\rm EJR}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
\]

and $s(N,W_{2})=58$ is attainable.

Hence, on the usual strict $>$ blocking definition,

\[
s(N,W_{1})=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})=58,\qquad
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

the cheapest core committee gives $N$ $65$ approvals, $8\cdot7+9$,
whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$ only $58$ approvals,
$8\cdot6+10$.  With the non-strict $\ge$ version of the $s=8$ block the
formal lower bound is $8t+p\ge64$, i.e. the familiar weak-core value
$s_{c}^{\ge}=64$ and the quoted $64/58=32/29$ ratio. ∎

For $i\in N$ put $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$,
$U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $t=|W\cap C|$,
$p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$ and $q=|W\cap\{25,\dots ,32\}|$.
$|W|=20$ gives

$ t+p+q=20,\qquad 0\le u_{i}\le2,\qquad q\ge4 $

and for $i\in N$

$v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}$,
$s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q       \tag{1}
$

Let $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $|X|=2s$ and $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$.
$t_{X}\le\min \{8,2s\}$ and a strict improvement of every $i\in S$
needs

$u_{iX}\ge t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1$,
$\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s-t_{X}$.

Hence a strict block exists iff

$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}       \tag{2}
$

for some admissible $t_{X}$.  The right hand side is maximal for
$t_{X}=\min\{8,2s\}$.  For $s\ge4$, $t_{X}=8$ and with $d_{i}=t+u_{i}-7$

$\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}\le 2s-8 $

is the blocking condition.  For $t\le6$ (2) is always satisfied for
$S=N$, so $t\ge7$.

For $t=7$ we have $d_{i}=u_{i}$ and (2) becomes

$P_{S}:=\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}\le 2s-8 , \qquad s\ge4,$

i.e. $W$ is $N$–core iff

$P_{S}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,|S|=s\ge4$,                     \tag{3}
$

in particular $p=P_{N}>8$.  With $q\ge4$, $p=13-q$, so $p>8$ forces
$q=4$ and $p\ge9$.  With $p=9$, e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and
$u_{i}=2$ for one voter,

$m_{s}:=\min_{|S|=s}P_{S}=s$ for $s\le7$ and $m_{8}=9$,

so that $m_{s}\ge2s-7>2s-8$ for every $s\ge4$.  Hence (3) is satisfied,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$ can be met with $q_{9}=q_{10}=2$ and no
$S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve.  On the
other hand $p=8$ gives $P_{N}=8$ and $N$ itself blocks $W$ with
$X=C\cup\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$, $t_{X}=8$, $\sum u_{iX}=8$.  Hence the
cheapest strict proportional core is

$t_{c}=7$, $q_{c}=4$, $p_{c}=9$,
$s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c}$,

and up to symmetry $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and $v_{i}=9$ for one
voter.  With $t=8$ the cheapest strict core is $p_{c}=1$, $q_{c}=11$,
$s_{c}=65$ as well, so $s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65$.

For EJR $\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)=C$, $|C|=8$, so $S\subset N$ is
$\ell$–cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.
Hence for $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$, $v_{(1)}\le\ldots\le v_{(8)}$,

$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad1\le s\le8,$
and $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.

Hence $v_{(4)}\ge8$ and $v_{i}\le t+2$.  The smallest possible $t$ is
$t_{e}=6$, whence $u_{(4)}\ge2$.  The cheapest distribution is
$u_{i}=2$ for five voters and $u_{i}=0$ for three voters,
$p_{e}=10$, $q_{e}=20-6-10=4$.  Then

$v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ for all $s$ and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$,

so EJR is met and

$s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e}$,

and $t<6$ is impossible.  Hence the cheapest EJR committee gives

$s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58$.

In the usual strict $>$ improvement sense

$s(N,W_{1})=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})=58,\qquad
\displaystyle\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,$

i.e. the cheapest core committee forces $N$ to obtain $65$ approvals,
$8\cdot7+9$, whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$ only
$58$ approvals, $8\cdot6+10$.  The $8t+p\ge64$ off–by–one weak
formulation gives the familiar $t_{c}=7,p_{c}=8,q_{c}=5$,
$s_{c}^{\ge}=64$ and the often quoted weak ratio $64/58=32/29$. ∎

$s_e=8\cdot6+10=58$, $v_i=8$ for five voters, $v_i=6$ for three, $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$. $t<6$ impossible. Hence $s(N,W_2)_{\min}=58$ is uncontested.

Core split remains. Strict $>$ blocking. For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $|X|=2s$, $t_X=|X\cap C|$. Strict block needs $t_X+u_{iX}>t+u_i$. Max $t_X=\min\{8,2s\}$. For $s\ge4$ take $t_X=8$, block condition is $\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}>2s-8$. In particular $t\ge7$; $t\le6$ is blocked by $N$.

For $t=7$, $\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}=u_i$, so core needs $\sum_{i\in S}u_i>2s-8$ $\forall s\ge4$, i.e. $p>8$. With $q\ge4$, $p=13-q$, so $q=4$ and $p\ge9$. Smallest feasible is $t_c=7$, $q_c=4$, $p_c=9$, e.g. $u_i=1$ for seven voters and $u_i=2$ for one voter. Then $v_i=8$ or $9$, $\sum_{S}u_i>2s-8$ for all $s\ge4$, singleton quotas met. $s_c=8\cdot7+9=65$. $p=8$ is blocked by $N$, $t=6$ blocked. $t=8,p=1,q=11$ gives same $s=65$. Hence strict proportional core minimum is $65$.

The weak $\ge$ formulation gives the off-by-one $8t+p\ge64$, i.e. the quoted $t=7,p=8,q=5$ point with $s_c^{\ge}=64$. Round-2 colleagues 1,5,7,9,14,14 push the $64/58=32/29$ weak-core value, often mis-stating $t=8,p=1$ as $64$. Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 keep the strict $65/58$ derivation and note the $64/58$ weak variant. Colleague 13’s $16/58$ proportional-union reading is not the approval core defined here.

Current working belief: strict core definition gives $s(N,W_1)=65$, $s(N,W_2)=58$, ratio $65/58\approx1.12$, with the familiar weak-core literature figure $64/58=32/29$ noted as the $8t+p\ge64$ off-by-one convention. Unresolved is whether the problem setter intends strict $>$ or the weak $\ge$ core; the $58$ EJR floor is invariant.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The eight voters N share C={1..8}. For i∈N, U_i are the two private approvals, |U_i|=2, disjoint. Let t=|W∩C|, u_i=|W∩U_i|, p=∑u_i, q=|W∩{25..32}|. |W|=20 gives t+p+q=20, q≥4 from |A(9)∩W|≥2,|A(10)∩W|≥2, so t+p≤16. v_i=t+u_i, s(N,W)=∑v_i=8t+p=7t+20−q.

EJR is stable. ∩_{i∈S}A(i)=C, |C|=8, so S⊂N is ℓ-cohesive iff |S|≥ℓ/2 for ℓ≤8. With v_i=t+u_i ordered, EJR is v_(s)≥min{8,2s} and |A(9)∩W|,|A(10)∩W|≥2. Binding is v_(4)≥8. v_i≤t+2 ⇒ t≥6. t=6 forces u_(4)≥2, i.e. at least five voters have u_i=2. Minimum p with that is p_e=10, e.g. five voters u_i=2, three voters u_i=0. Then q_e=20−6−10=4, v_i=8 for five voters, v_i=6 for three voters, and EJR holds. Hence s_e=8·6+10=58=7·6+20−4 is attainable and minimal; no t<6 works. s(N,W2)_min=58 is unanimous across all contributions.

Core. For S⊂N, |S|=s, a deviation X of size 2s can be taken with t_X=8 for s≥4. Strict improvement v_i^X>t+u_i needs u_iX≥t+u_i−t_X+1. With t≤6 the N-coalition blocks. t≥7 is necessary.

For t=7, a strict block of S requires ∑_{i∈S}u_i ≤2s−8. Hence N-core requires p>8 and for every s≥4, P_S>2s−8. With q≥4, p=13−q. p>8 forces q=4 and p≥9. The smallest feasible strict point is t_c=7,q_c=4,p_c=9, e.g. seven voters u_i=1 and one voter u_i=2, giving v_i=8/9 and s_c=56+9=65. t=7,p=8 is blocked by N with X=C∪∪U_i; t=6 is blocked. t=8,p=1 also gives s=65 and is strict core, e.g. t=8,u_i=1 for one voter, s=65. Hence on the usual strict > blocking convention s(N,W1)_min^strict=65.

The frequently quoted 64 value is the weak ≥ version of the s=8 block. With non-strict blocking the condition for S=N becomes p≥8, and the off-by-one point t=7,p=8,q=5 gives s=8·7+8=64. This is the 32/29=64/58 ratio cited by colleagues 1,5,7,9,14 etc., and it coincides with the t=8,p=0 mis-evaluation. The proportional-core quota |W∩∪A(i)|≥2|S| used by colleagues 2,6 gives the even weaker 16/58 figure.

Current status: EJR floor 58 is solid. Core minimum is 65 under strict > improvement and 64 under the weak ≥ convention. The deliberation is split between the strict 65/58≈1.12 reading and the weak 64/58=32/29 reading; the EJR part is settled.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The profile is $k=20$, $n=10$, $N=\{1..8\}$, $C=\{1..8\}$, $U_i=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_i|=2$, $Q=\{25..32\}$, $|Q|=8$. Write $t=|W\cap C|$, $u_i=|W\cap U_i|$, $p=\sum_i u_i$, $q=|W\cap Q|$. Then $|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_i\le2$, $q\ge4$ from $|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$, and $q\le8$.
For $i\in N$ $v_i=t+u_i$ and
$s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_i=8t+p=7t+20-q$.

Core. For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $|X|=2s$, $t_X=|X\cap C|\le\min\{8,2s\}$. Strict improvement needs $t_X+u_{iX}>t+u_i\ \forall i\in S$. With $t_X=\min\{8,2s\}$ the condition is $\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_i-t_X+1\}>2s-t_X$. For $s\ge4$, $t_X=8$.

$t\le6$ is blocked by $S=N$. Hence $t\ge7$.
For $t=7$, $\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}=u_i$ and strict $N$–core needs $p>8$. With $t+p+q=20$, $q\ge4$, $p=13-q$, so $p>8\iff q=4$ and $p\ge9$. The cheapest strict distribution is $p_c=9$, e.g. $u_i=1$ for seven voters and $u_i=2$ for one, $q_c=4$, $v_i=8$ or $9$. Then $\sum_{S}u_i>2s-8$ for all $s\ge4$ and no $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve. Hence
$s_c^{\min}=8\cdot7+9=65=7\cdot7+20-4$.
$t=8$ would need $q=12-p\le8\Rightarrow p\ge4$ and $s\ge68>65$. The often quoted $t=8,p=1$ point is infeasible because it would require $q=11>8$.

Weak $\ge$ version allows $p\ge8$, i.e. $t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_c^{\ge}=64$. This is the off-by-one $8t+p\ge64$ bound.

EJR. $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$. With $v_i=t+u_i$ ordered $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$, in particular $v_{(4)}\ge8$. Hence $t\ge6$ and for $t=6$ need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters with $u_i=2$. The cheapest EJR is
$t_e=6$, $p_e=10$ $u_i=2$ for five voters, $u_i=0$ for three, $q_e=4$, $v_i=8$ five times, $v_i=6$ three times.
$s_e^{\min}=8\cdot6+10=58=7\cdot6+20-4$ and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$. The EJR floor $58$ is stable under both core conventions.

Hence under the usual strict $>$ blocking definition
$s(N,W_1)_{\min}=65$, $s(N,W_2)_{\min}=58$, ratio $65/58$.
With the weak $\ge$ formulation of the core the conventionally quoted minimum is $s(N,W_1)^{\ge}=64$, $s(N,W_2)=58$, ratio $64/58=32/29$.

Disagreements in round 2: several colleagues propose a $t=8,p=1$ core with $s=64$, which violates $q\le8$; the $16/58$ claim uses the proportional-quota $ |W\cap\bigcup A(i)|\ge2|S|$ version of the core, a different definition. The strict-improvement analysis is consistent across Colleagues 10, 11, 12, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8. The remaining unresolved issue is whether the problem intends strict $>$ or weak $\ge$ core. Strict is the standard definition; weak gives the familiar $32/29$ figure.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The profile is $C=\{1..8\}$, $U_i$ two private seats for $i\in N$, $Q=\{25..32\}$ for voters 9,10. Put $t=|W\cap C|$, $u_i=|W\cap U_i|$, $p=\sum_i u_i$, $q=|W\cap Q|$. $|W|=20$ gives $t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_i\le2$, $q\ge4$ from $|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.
$v_i=t+u_i$, $s(N,W)=\sum_i v_i=8t+p=7t+20-q$.

EJR. $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$. Hence $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ and in particular $v_{(4)}\ge8$. This forces $t\ge6$ and with $t=6$ $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters have $u_i=2$. The cheapest realisation is
$t_e=6$, $u_i=2$ for five voters, $u_i=0$ for three voters, $p_e=10$, $q_e=4$.
Then $v_i=8$ five times, $v_i=6$ three times, $s_e=8t_e+p_e=48+10=58=7t_e+20-q_e$.
This EJR floor is unanimously accepted in round 2; $t<6$ is impossible.

Core, strict $>$.
For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, a deviation $X$, $|X|=2s$, $t_X=|X\cap C|$. Strict improvement is $t_X+u_{iX}>t+u_i$ $\forall i\in S$, i.e. $\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_i-t_X+1\}\le2s-t_X$. With $s\ge4$ the best $t_X$ is $8$. Hence a block exists iff
$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}\le 2s-8$.
In particular for $S=N$, $s=8$, $\sum_i\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}\le8$.

$t\le6$ is blocked. For $t=7$, $\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}=u_i$ and $N$ blocks iff $p\le8$; for any four-subset the condition is $\sum_{S}u_i>2s-8$. Hence the strict $N$-core needs $p>8$. With $q\ge4$, $p=13-q$, so $p>8$ forces $q=4$, $p\ge9$. The smallest admissible distribution is $t_c=7$, $q_c=4$, $p_c=9$, e.g. seven voters $u_i=1$ and one voter $u_i=2$, giving $v_i=8$ or $9$ and $\sum_Su_i>2|S|-8$ for all $|S|\ge4$. Then $s_c=8t_c+p_c=56+9=65=7t_c+20-q_c$. $t=8$ forces $p=12-q\ge4$, $q\le8$, so $s\ge64+p\ge68>65$. The often quoted $t=8,p=1,q=11$ is infeasible because $q\le|Q|=8$.

Hence on the usual strict $>$ improvement definition
$s(N,W_1)_{\min}=65$, $s(N,W_2)_{\min}=58$, ratio $65/58\approx1.12$.

Weak / non-strict formulation.
With the weak $\ge$ block the off-by-one bound is $8t+p\ge64$. The conventionally quoted weak point is $t=7$, $p=8$, $q=5$, $s_c^{\ge}=64$, and $s_e=58$, giving $64/58=32/29$. This is the 64 figure repeatedly cited by colleagues 1,5,7,9,14. The $t=8,p=1$ relaxation is infeasible under the actual candidate universe, so the strict minimum stays at 65.

The 16-approval proportional core claimed by colleagues 2,6,13 uses the union quota $|W\cap\bigcup_{i\in T}A(i)|\ge2|T|$ and ignores the per-voter strict improvement requirement; it is not the core used in the question. Unresolved in the discussion is whether the problem intends the strict $>$ core or the weak $\ge$ version; the mathematically consistent strict core minimum is 65 with EJR minimum 58.

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The profile is k=20, n=10, N={1..8}, C={1..8}, U_i the two private approvals of i,
t=|W∩C|, u_i=|W∩U_i|, p=∑u_i, q=|W∩{25..32}|, |W|=t+p+q=20, q≥4.
v_i=t+u_i, s(N,W)=∑v_i=8t+p=7t+20−q.

Strict proportional core. For S⊂N, |S|=s, |X|=2s, t_X=|X∩C|≤min{8,2s}.
A strict block needs t_X+u_{iX}>t+u_i ∀i∈S, i.e.
∑_{i∈S}max{0,t+u_i−t_X+1}≤2s−t_X.
The best t_X is min{8,2s}. For s≥4 t_X=8 and the condition is

t≤6 is blocked. t=7 gives max{0,t+u_i−7}=u_i and N blocks iff p≤8.

Then s_c=8·7+9=65=7·7+20−4. The symmetric point t=8,p=1,q=11 also gives

EJR. ∩_{i∈S}A(i)=C, |C|=8. S is ℓ-cohesive iff |S|≥⌈ℓ/2⌉ for ℓ≤8.
With v_i=t+u_i ordered v_(s)≥min{8,2s}, s=1..8 and |A(9)∩W|,|A(10)∩W|≥2.
Binding is v_(4)≥8. v_i≤t+2 ⇒ t≥6. For t=6 need u_(4)≥2, i.e. at least

Then v_i=8 for five voters, v_i=6 for three voters, v_(s)≥min{8,2s} holds.
s_e=8·6+10=58=7·6+20−4. t<6 impossible. Hence s_EJR^min=58 is stable.

Hence on the usual strict > improvement core
s_core^min(N)=65, s_EJR^min(N)=58, ratio=65/58≈1.12.
The familiar weak-core off-by-one is s_c^≥=64, ratio 64/58=32/29,
attained e.g. t=7,p=8,q=5 in the weak ≥ version. The union-size
proportional core gives the 16 vs 58, 8/29, variant.

Current round disagreement is exactly the strict vs weak core convention
and the arithmetic slip 8·8+1=65 vs 64. The strict minimum is 65 vs 58.
The 64/58=32/29 figure is the weak ≥ block / non-strict core
convention repeatedly cited by colleagues 1,5,7,9,14. The 16/58
