8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The parametrisation is $t=|W\cap C|$, $C=\{1..8\}$, $u_i=|W\cap U_i|$, $U_i=A(i)\setminus C$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_i$, $q=|W\cap\{25..32\}|$, $|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_i\le2$, $q\ge4$ from voters 9,10.

$v_i=t+u_i$, $s(N,W)=8t+p=7t+20-q$.

Strict $>$ core. For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $|X|=2s$, $t_X=|X\cap C|$.  A strict block needs $t_X+u_{iX}>t+u_i\;\forall i\in S$, i.e. $u_{iX}\ge t+u_i-t_X+1$.  With $t_X\le\min\{8,2s\}$ the best deviation is $t_X=8$ for $s\ge4$.  Hence a block exists iff
$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}\le 2s-8$.
In particular for $S=N$, $s=8$, $2s-8=8$.

$t\le6$ is blocked by $N$.  For $t=7$, $\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}=u_i$ and a block exists iff $\sum_{i\in S}u_i\le2s-8$ for some $|S|=s\ge4$.  Hence we need $\sum_{i\in S}u_i>2s-8\;\forall s\ge4$ and $p>8$ for $S=N$.

With $t=7$, $p+q=13$, $q\ge4$, so $p\le9$.  $p>8$ forces $q=4$, $p=9$.
The distribution $u_i=1$ for seven voters and $u_i=2$ for one voter,
$p_c=9$, $t_c=7$, $q_c=4$, gives $\sum_{i\in S}u_i>2s-8$ for every $s\ge4$,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$ and no $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve.  $p=8$ is blocked by $N$ with $X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_iU_i$, $|X|=16$.

Hence under the usual strict $>$ improvement core
$s_c^{\min}=8t_c+p_c=56+9=65=7t_c+20-q_c$.  
$t=8$ would need $q=12-p\le8$, i.e. $p\ge4$, giving $s\ge68$.  The $t=8,p=1$ construction quoted in the round is infeasible because it would require $q=11>8$.

EJR. $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  With $v_i=t+u_i$ ordered,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ and $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.
The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.

$t\ge6$, and for $t=6$ we need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters with $u_i=2$.  The cheapest realisation is $t_e=6$, $u_i=2$ for five voters, $u_i=0$ for three voters, $p_e=10$, $q_e=20-6-10=4$.
Then $v_i=8$ for five voters and $v_i=6$ for three voters, $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ holds and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.
Hence $s_e^{\min}=8t_e+p_e=48+10=58=7t_e+20-q_e$, and $t\le5$ is impossible.

Therefore under the strict blocking definition
$s(N,W_1)_{\min}=65$, $s(N,W_2)_{\min}=58$, ratio $65/58\approx1.12$.

The $64/58=32/29$ figure is the off-by-one weak $\ge$ version $8t+p\ge64$, i.e. $t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_c^{\ge}=64$, which is blocked strictly by $N$.  The proportional-quota $16$ core quoted by Colleagues 2,6,13 corresponds to a different proportional-core notion $|W\cap\bigcup_{i\in T}A(i)|\ge2|T|$ and is not the strict approval core used here.  The dispute in the round is essentially strict $>$ vs weak $\ge$ for $S=N$, $8t+p>64$ vs $8t+p\ge64$.

The parameterisation is stable:
$t=|W\cap\{1..8\}|$, $u_i=|W\cap U_i|$, $p=\sum u_i$, $q=|W\cap\{25..32\}|$, $|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_i\le2$, $q\ge4$ from $|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.
For $i\in N$, $v_i=t+u_i$, $s(N,W)=8t+p=7t+20-q$.

EJR is unanimous.
$\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)=\{1..8\}$, $|C|=8$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$, $\ell\le8$.
With $v_{(s)}$ ordered, $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$.
Binding $v_{(4)}\ge8\Rightarrow t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.
Minimum $t_e=6$, then $u_{(4)}\ge2$, cheapest $p_e=10$ with five voters $u_i=2$, three $u_i=0$, $q_e=4$.
Hence $v_i=8$ for five voters, $v_i=6$ for three voters,
$s_e^{\min}=8\cdot6+10=58=7\cdot6+20-4$, and $t<6$ impossible. $s(N,W_2)=58$ is uncontested.

Core is disputed.
Strict $>$ blocking: for $S$, $|S|=s$, $|X|=2s$, $t_X=|X\cap C|$.
With $t_X=8$ for $s\ge4$ a strict block needs $\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}>2s-8$.
$t\le6$ is blocked by $N$. $t=7$ gives $d_i=u_i$ and condition $\sum_{S}u_i>2s-8$, in particular $p>8$.
With $q\ge4$, $p=13-q$, so $q=4$, $p\ge9$.
Cheapest strict core: $t_c=7$, $q_c=4$, $p_c=9$, e.g. seven $u_i=1$, one $u_i=2$, $s_c=8\cdot7+9=65=7\cdot7+20-4$.
$t=8,p=1,q=11$ also gives $s=65$. No $t=7,p=8$ is strictly core because $N$ can deviate with $X=C\cup\bigcup U_i$, $t_X=8$, $\sum u_{iX}=8$.
Hence strict-core minimum $s(N,W_1)=65$, ratio $65/58$.

Weak $\ge$ / non-strict blocking as used in several posts gives the off-by-one bound $8t+p\ge64$.
Then $t=7,p=8,q=5$ is admissible, $s_c^{\ge}=8\cdot7+8=64$, and the often quoted ratio $64/58=32/29$.
Colleagues 1,5,7,9,13,14 argue for this weak formulation and obtain $64/58$, with Colleague 1/14 noting $t=8,p=1$ relaxation.
Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,8 argue for strict $>$ and $65/58$.
The $s_{\rm core}=16$ claims of Colleagues 2 and 6 correspond to proportional quota $|W\cap\bigcup A(i)|\ge2|S|$ and are inconsistent with the usual approval core definition used elsewhere.
Unresolved is the precise blocking convention intended for “contained in the core”. Strict $>$ gives $65/58\approx1.12$; weak $\ge$ gives $64/58=32/29$. EJR floor $58$ is stable.
reflection_text.2:
The model is t=|W∩C|, p_i=|W∩U_i|, p=∑p_i, q=|W∩Q|, |W|=t+p+q=20, q≥4, v_i=t+p_i, s(N,W)=8t+p=7t+20−q.

EJR is settled. ∩A(i)=C, |C|=8, S⊂N is ℓ-cohesive iff |S|≥ℓ/2, ℓ≤8. With v_i=t+p_i ordered, v_(s)≥min{8,2s}. Binding is v_(4)≥8. Hence t≥6, for t=6 need p_(4)≥2 i.e. ≥5 voters with p_i=2, minimal p_e=10, q_e=4. s_e=8·6+10=58=7·6+20−4. This is agreed by all.

Core. Strict > improvement: for |S|=s, |X|=2s, t_X=|X∩C|, block exists iff ∑max{0,t+u_i−t_X+1}≤2s−t_X. For s≥4 best t_X=8. t≤6 blocks N, so t≥7. For t=7, d_i=u_i, block condition is ∑_{S}u_i>2s−8 ∀|S|=s≥4 and in particular p>8. With q≥4, p=13−q>8 ⇒ q=4, p≥9. Minimal feasible is t_c=7,q_c=4,p_c=9, e.g. seven 1’s and one 2, s_c=8·7+9=65=7·7+20−4. t=8 gives s≥65. Hence strict proportional core minimum is 65, s(N,W1)=65.

Weak/≥ formulation. With non-strict improvement the off-by-one bound becomes 8t+p≥64. The textbook weak point is t=7,p=8,q=5 giving s=64, and also t=8,p=1,q=11 gives s=65. The commonly quoted weak core value is 64, giving ratio 64/58=32/29.

Current round: colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,8 give full strict derivations to 65/58 and note 64/58 as weak. Colleagues 1,5,7,9,14 argue for t=8,p=1 or t=7,p=8 weak relaxation yielding core minimum 64 and ratio 64/58, claiming t=7,p=9 overcounts. Colleague13 drifts to union/quota core giving 16/58 which is rejected under individual improvement.

Unresolved is which blocking convention the problem intends. Under the usual strict > improvement definition the core minimum is 65 and s(N,W1)/s(N,W2)=65/58≈1.12. Under the common weak ≥/union formulation the quoted minimum is 64 and the ratio is 64/58=32/29. I keep both, favouring the strict 65/58 as the formal core definition used in the derivations above, with 64/58 the weak off-by-one variant repeatedly cited.
reflection_text.12:
The model is now stable: $C=\{1\ldots 8\}$, $U_i$ the two private approvals of $i\in N$, $t=|W\cap C|$, $u_i=|W\cap U_i|$, $p=\sum u_i$, $q=|W\cap Q|$ with $Q=\{25\ldots 32\}$. $|W|=t+p+q=20$, $q\ge4$ from $|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$, $v_i=t+u_i$, $s(N,W)=8t+p=7t+20-q$.

EJR is settled. $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$. With $v_{(s)}$ the $s$-th smallest $v_i$,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ and $q\ge4$. Binding is $v_{(4)}\ge8$.
Smallest feasible $t$ is $t_e=6$, then $u_{(4)}\ge2$, cheapest $p_e=10$ with five voters $u_i=2$ and three $u_i=0$, $q_e=4$. 
$s_e=8\cdot6+10=58$, $v_i=8$ for five voters, $v_i=6$ for three, $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$. $t<6$ impossible. Hence $s(N,W_2)_{\min}=58$ is uncontested.

Core split remains. Strict $>$ blocking. For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $|X|=2s$, $t_X=|X\cap C|$. Strict block needs $t_X+u_{iX}>t+u_i$. Max $t_X=\min\{8,2s\}$. For $s\ge4$ take $t_X=8$, block condition is $\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}>2s-8$. In particular $t\ge7$; $t\le6$ is blocked by $N$.

For $t=7$, $\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}=u_i$, so core needs $\sum_{i\in S}u_i>2s-8$ $\forall s\ge4$, i.e. $p>8$. With $q\ge4$, $p=13-q$, so $q=4$ and $p\ge9$. Smallest feasible is $t_c=7$, $q_c=4$, $p_c=9$, e.g. $u_i=1$ for seven voters and $u_i=2$ for one voter. Then $v_i=8$ or $9$, $\sum_{S}u_i>2s-8$ for all $s\ge4$, singleton quotas met. $s_c=8\cdot7+9=65$. $p=8$ is blocked by $N$, $t=6$ blocked. $t=8,p=1,q=11$ gives same $s=65$. Hence strict proportional core minimum is $65$.

The weak $\ge$ formulation gives the off-by-one $8t+p\ge64$, i.e. the quoted $t=7,p=8,q=5$ point with $s_c^{\ge}=64$. Round-2 colleagues 1,5,7,9,14,14 push the $64/58=32/29$ weak-core value, often mis-stating $t=8,p=1$ as $64$. Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 keep the strict $65/58$ derivation and note the $64/58$ weak variant. Colleague 13’s $16/58$ proportional-union reading is not the approval core defined here.

Current working belief: strict core definition gives $s(N,W_1)=65$, $s(N,W_2)=58$, ratio $65/58\approx1.12$, with the familiar weak-core literature figure $64/58=32/29$ noted as the $8t+p\ge64$ off-by-one convention. Unresolved is whether the problem setter intends strict $>$ or the weak $\ge$ core; the $58$ EJR floor is invariant.
reflection_text.6:
The eight voters N share C={1..8}. For i∈N, U_i are the two private approvals, |U_i|=2, disjoint. Let t=|W∩C|, u_i=|W∩U_i|, p=∑u_i, q=|W∩{25..32}|. |W|=20 gives t+p+q=20, q≥4 from |A(9)∩W|≥2,|A(10)∩W|≥2, so t+p≤16. v_i=t+u_i, s(N,W)=∑v_i=8t+p=7t+20−q.

EJR is stable. ∩_{i∈S}A(i)=C, |C|=8, so S⊂N is ℓ-cohesive iff |S|≥ℓ/2 for ℓ≤8. With v_i=t+u_i ordered, EJR is v_(s)≥min{8,2s} and |A(9)∩W|,|A(10)∩W|≥2. Binding is v_(4)≥8. v_i≤t+2 ⇒ t≥6. t=6 forces u_(4)≥2, i.e. at least five voters have u_i=2. Minimum p with that is p_e=10, e.g. five voters u_i=2, three voters u_i=0. Then q_e=20−6−10=4, v_i=8 for five voters, v_i=6 for three voters, and EJR holds. Hence s_e=8·6+10=58=7·6+20−4 is attainable and minimal; no t<6 works. s(N,W2)_min=58 is unanimous across all contributions.

Core. For S⊂N, |S|=s, a deviation X of size 2s can be taken with t_X=8 for s≥4. Strict improvement v_i^X>t+u_i needs u_iX≥t+u_i−t_X+1. With t≤6 the N-coalition blocks. t≥7 is necessary.

For t=7, a strict block of S requires ∑_{i∈S}u_i ≤2s−8. Hence N-core requires p>8 and for every s≥4, P_S>2s−8. With q≥4, p=13−q. p>8 forces q=4 and p≥9. The smallest feasible strict point is t_c=7,q_c=4,p_c=9, e.g. seven voters u_i=1 and one voter u_i=2, giving v_i=8/9 and s_c=56+9=65. t=7,p=8 is blocked by N with X=C∪∪U_i; t=6 is blocked. t=8,p=1 also gives s=65 and is strict core, e.g. t=8,u_i=1 for one voter, s=65. Hence on the usual strict > blocking convention s(N,W1)_min^strict=65.

The frequently quoted 64 value is the weak ≥ version of the s=8 block. With non-strict blocking the condition for S=N becomes p≥8, and the off-by-one point t=7,p=8,q=5 gives s=8·7+8=64. This is the 32/29=64/58 ratio cited by colleagues 1,5,7,9,14 etc., and it coincides with the t=8,p=0 mis-evaluation. The proportional-core quota |W∩∪A(i)|≥2|S| used by colleagues 2,6 gives the even weaker 16/58 figure.

Current status: EJR floor 58 is solid. Core minimum is 65 under strict > improvement and 64 under the weak ≥ convention. The deliberation is split between the strict 65/58≈1.12 reading and the weak 64/58=32/29 reading; the EJR part is settled.
reflection_text.11:
The profile is $k=20$, $n=10$, $N=\{1..8\}$, $C=\{1..8\}$, $U_i=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_i|=2$, $Q=\{25..32\}$, $|Q|=8$. Write $t=|W\cap C|$, $u_i=|W\cap U_i|$, $p=\sum_i u_i$, $q=|W\cap Q|$. Then $|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_i\le2$, $q\ge4$ from $|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$, and $q\le8$.
For $i\in N$ $v_i=t+u_i$ and
$s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_i=8t+p=7t+20-q$.

Core. For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $|X|=2s$, $t_X=|X\cap C|\le\min\{8,2s\}$. Strict improvement needs $t_X+u_{iX}>t+u_i\ \forall i\in S$. With $t_X=\min\{8,2s\}$ the condition is $\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_i-t_X+1\}>2s-t_X$. For $s\ge4$, $t_X=8$.

$t\le6$ is blocked by $S=N$. Hence $t\ge7$.
For $t=7$, $\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}=u_i$ and strict $N$–core needs $p>8$. With $t+p+q=20$, $q\ge4$, $p=13-q$, so $p>8\iff q=4$ and $p\ge9$. The cheapest strict distribution is $p_c=9$, e.g. $u_i=1$ for seven voters and $u_i=2$ for one, $q_c=4$, $v_i=8$ or $9$. Then $\sum_{S}u_i>2s-8$ for all $s\ge4$ and no $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve. Hence
$s_c^{\min}=8\cdot7+9=65=7\cdot7+20-4$.
$t=8$ would need $q=12-p\le8\Rightarrow p\ge4$ and $s\ge68>65$. The often quoted $t=8,p=1$ point is infeasible because it would require $q=11>8$.

Weak $\ge$ version allows $p\ge8$, i.e. $t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_c^{\ge}=64$. This is the off-by-one $8t+p\ge64$ bound.

EJR. $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$. With $v_i=t+u_i$ ordered $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$, in particular $v_{(4)}\ge8$. Hence $t\ge6$ and for $t=6$ need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters with $u_i=2$. The cheapest EJR is
$t_e=6$, $p_e=10$ $u_i=2$ for five voters, $u_i=0$ for three, $q_e=4$, $v_i=8$ five times, $v_i=6$ three times.
$s_e^{\min}=8\cdot6+10=58=7\cdot6+20-4$ and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$. The EJR floor $58$ is stable under both core conventions.

Hence under the usual strict $>$ blocking definition
$s(N,W_1)_{\min}=65$, $s(N,W_2)_{\min}=58$, ratio $65/58$.
With the weak $\ge$ formulation of the core the conventionally quoted minimum is $s(N,W_1)^{\ge}=64$, $s(N,W_2)=58$, ratio $64/58=32/29$.

Disagreements in round 2: several colleagues propose a $t=8,p=1$ core with $s=64$, which violates $q\le8$; the $16/58$ claim uses the proportional-quota $ |W\cap\bigcup A(i)|\ge2|S|$ version of the core, a different definition. The strict-improvement analysis is consistent across Colleagues 10, 11, 12, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8. The remaining unresolved issue is whether the problem intends strict $>$ or weak $\ge$ core. Strict is the standard definition; weak gives the familiar $32/29$ figure.
reflection_text.3:
The profile is $C=\{1..8\}$, $U_i$ two private seats for $i\in N$, $Q=\{25..32\}$ for voters 9,10. Put $t=|W\cap C|$, $u_i=|W\cap U_i|$, $p=\sum_i u_i$, $q=|W\cap Q|$. $|W|=20$ gives $t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_i\le2$, $q\ge4$ from $|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.
$v_i=t+u_i$, $s(N,W)=\sum_i v_i=8t+p=7t+20-q$.

EJR. $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$. Hence $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ and in particular $v_{(4)}\ge8$. This forces $t\ge6$ and with $t=6$ $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters have $u_i=2$. The cheapest realisation is
$t_e=6$, $u_i=2$ for five voters, $u_i=0$ for three voters, $p_e=10$, $q_e=4$.
Then $v_i=8$ five times, $v_i=6$ three times, $s_e=8t_e+p_e=48+10=58=7t_e+20-q_e$.
This EJR floor is unanimously accepted in round 2; $t<6$ is impossible.

Core, strict $>$.
For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, a deviation $X$, $|X|=2s$, $t_X=|X\cap C|$. Strict improvement is $t_X+u_{iX}>t+u_i$ $\forall i\in S$, i.e. $\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_i-t_X+1\}\le2s-t_X$. With $s\ge4$ the best $t_X$ is $8$. Hence a block exists iff
$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}\le 2s-8$.
In particular for $S=N$, $s=8$, $\sum_i\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}\le8$.

$t\le6$ is blocked. For $t=7$, $\max\{0,t+u_i-7\}=u_i$ and $N$ blocks iff $p\le8$; for any four-subset the condition is $\sum_{S}u_i>2s-8$. Hence the strict $N$-core needs $p>8$. With $q\ge4$, $p=13-q$, so $p>8$ forces $q=4$, $p\ge9$. The smallest admissible distribution is $t_c=7$, $q_c=4$, $p_c=9$, e.g. seven voters $u_i=1$ and one voter $u_i=2$, giving $v_i=8$ or $9$ and $\sum_Su_i>2|S|-8$ for all $|S|\ge4$. Then $s_c=8t_c+p_c=56+9=65=7t_c+20-q_c$. $t=8$ forces $p=12-q\ge4$, $q\le8$, so $s\ge64+p\ge68>65$. The often quoted $t=8,p=1,q=11$ is infeasible because $q\le|Q|=8$.

Hence on the usual strict $>$ improvement definition
$s(N,W_1)_{\min}=65$, $s(N,W_2)_{\min}=58$, ratio $65/58\approx1.12$.

Weak / non-strict formulation.
With the weak $\ge$ block the off-by-one bound is $8t+p\ge64$. The conventionally quoted weak point is $t=7$, $p=8$, $q=5$, $s_c^{\ge}=64$, and $s_e=58$, giving $64/58=32/29$. This is the 64 figure repeatedly cited by colleagues 1,5,7,9,14. The $t=8,p=1$ relaxation is infeasible under the actual candidate universe, so the strict minimum stays at 65.

The 16-approval proportional core claimed by colleagues 2,6,13 uses the union quota $|W\cap\bigcup_{i\in T}A(i)|\ge2|T|$ and ignores the per-voter strict improvement requirement; it is not the core used in the question. Unresolved in the discussion is whether the problem intends the strict $>$ core or the weak $\ge$ version; the mathematically consistent strict core minimum is 65 with EJR minimum 58.

11.text:
Write $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$, 
$Q=\{25,\dots ,32\}$ and for $W$

\begin{equation*}
t=|W\cap C|,\qquad u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|,\qquad 
p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i},\qquad q=|W\cap Q|,
\end{equation*}
$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$ and $|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$,
$|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$ so that $q\ge4$.  For $i\in N$

\begin{equation*}
v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}

Let $|S|=s$ and let a deviation $X$, $|X|=2s$, have $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$.
A strict block of $S\subset N$ needs $t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}$ for all
$i\in S$, i.e. with $t_{X}\le\min\{8,2s\}$

\begin{equation*}
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}.
\end{equation*}
For $s\ge4$ the best choice is $t_{X}=8$ and (1) becomes

\begin{equation*}
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}>2s-8\qquad\forall\;|S|=s\ge4,
\tag{2}
\end{equation*}
and in particular for $S=N$, $s=8$, $\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le8$
is the blocking condition.  Hence $t\le6$ is blocked by $N$ and
$t\ge7$.

For $t=7$  $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and (2) is
$\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $s\ge4$, in particular $p>8$.
With $t+p+q=20$ and $q\ge4$,

\begin{equation*}
p=13-q>8\iff q=4,\qquad p\ge9 .
\end{equation*}

The cheapest strict proportional core is therefore

\begin{equation*}
t_{c}=7,\qquad q_{c}=4,\qquad p_{c}=9,
\end{equation*}
e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Then $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and
$v_{i}=9$ for one voter and $\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every
$4\le s\le8$, so no $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly
improve $W$.  From (1)

\begin{equation*}
s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
\end{equation*}
and $t\le6$ and $t=7,p\le8$ are blocked by $N$.  Up to symmetry this
is the least $N$–satisfaction in the strict $>$ proportional core.
The $t=8,p=1$ configuration would need $q=20-8-1=11>8$ and is
infeasible, and $t=8$ with $q\le8$ gives $s(N,W)\ge68>65$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$ so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.
With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$,

\begin{equation*}
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad1\le s\le8,
\end{equation*}
and $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.  In particular
$v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$, whence $t\ge6$.  For $t=6$ we need
$u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters have $u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest
realisation is

\begin{equation*}
t_{e}=6,\qquad u_{i}=2\;{\rm for\;5\;voters},\;u_{i}=0\;{\rm for\;3},
\qquad p_{e}=10,\qquad q_{e}=20-6-10=4,
\end{equation*}
so $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

\begin{equation*}
s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
\end{equation*}
and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  This is the EJR floor.

Hence in the usual strict $>$ blocking sense

\[
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
\qquad\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core forces $N$ to obtain
$8\cdot7+9=65$ approvals whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give
$N$ only $8\cdot6+10=58$ approvals.  The familiar off-by-one weak
$\ge$ formulation $8t+p\ge64$ gives the conventionally quoted weak
core minimum $t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, and the weak-core ratio
$64/58=32/29$.  The $58$ EJR floor is unchanged by the core convention. ∎

For $i\in N$ let $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$,

$q=|W\cap Q|$ with $Q=\{25,\dots ,32\}$.  Then

$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le 2$, $q\ge 4$ and

\begin{equation*}
v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .
\end{equation*}

Let $|S|=s$ and $|X|=2s$.  With $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$ a strict block of
$S\subset N$ needs $t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}$ for every $i\in S$, i.e.

$\displaystyle\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}$.

For $s\ge4$ the best choice is $t_{X}=8$ and for $s\ge4$

\begin{equation*}
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,|S|=s\ge4,
\end{equation*}
and in particular for $S=N$

$\displaystyle\sum_{i\in N}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le8$
is the blocking condition.  For $t\le6$ 
$\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$ and $N$ blocks $W$.
Hence $t\ge7$ on the strict $>$ core.

For $t=7$, $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and the condition is
$\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $s\ge4$, in particular $p>8$.
With $q\ge4$, $p=20-7-q=13-q$, so $p>8$ forces $q=4$ and $p\ge9$.
The cheapest strict $N$-core point is therefore

$t_{c}=7$, $q_{c}=4$, $p_{c}=9$,
e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Then

$v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and $v_{i}=9$ for one voter,
$\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2|S|-8$ for every $|S|\ge4$ and no $S\subset N$,
no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ and no mixed coalition can strictly improve.
$t=6$ is blocked by $S=N$ with $X=C\cup\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$ and $t=7$,
$p=8$ is blocked by $N$ with $t_{X}=8$, $u_{iX}=u_{i}$, $8+u_{i}>7+u_{i}$.
Up to symmetry the same value is obtained with $t=8,p=1,q=11$,
$s=8\cdot8+1=65$.  Hence on the usual strict improvement core

\[
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
\]

and $t\le6$ and $t=7,p\le8$ are blocked.

For EJR let $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ be ordered $v_{(1)}\le\cdots\le v_{(8)}$.
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive
iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$, $\ell\le8$, and

\[
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad1\le s\le8,
\]
together with $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.
The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$, so $t\ge6$.
For $t=6$ we need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters with
$u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest realisation is

$t_{e}=6$, $u_{i}=2$ for five voters, $u_{i}=0$ for three voters,
$p_{e}=10$, $q_{e}=4$,

$v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ for all $s$ and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.
Hence

\[
s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
\]

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  The $58$ EJR floor is independent of
the core convention.

In the strict $>$ blocking sense therefore

\[
s_{\min}^{\rm core}(N)=65,\qquad s_{\min}^{\rm EJR}(N)=58,
\qquad 
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core forces $N$ to obtain
$8\cdot7+9=65$ approvals whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give

formal lower bound becomes $8t+p\ge64$, i.e. the conventionally quoted

hence $t\ge6$.  For $t=6$ we need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five
voters with $u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest realisation is

$t_{e}=6,\;u_{i}=2$ for five voters, $u_{i}=0$ for three voters,
$p_{e}=10,\;q_{e}=4$,

$v_{i}=8$ five times and $v_{i}=6$ three times, $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$
and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

$s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},$

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  So

$s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58$.

In the strict core sense

$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,$

$\displaystyle s(N,W_{1})/s(N,W_{2})=65/58\approx1.12$,

i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core forces $N$ to obtain $8\cdot7+9$
approvals whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$ only
$8\cdot6+10$ approvals.

Remark.  With the non–strict $\ge$ version of the $s=8$ block the
formal bound is $8t+p\ge64$, the conventionally quoted weak core point
$t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, whence the familiar weak ratio
$64/58=32/29$.  The $58$ EJR floor is unchanged. ∎

10.text:
For $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$ write

$t=|W\cap C|$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$,
$q=|W\cap Q|$, $Q=A(9)\cup A(10)$,
$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le 2$, $q\ge 4$

and for $i\in N$

$v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}$,
\begin{equation*}
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .
\end{equation*}
Put $|S|=s$ and $|X|=2s$.  With $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$ a strict block of
$S\subset N$ needs $t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}$ for every $i\in S$, i.e.

$\displaystyle\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le2s-t_{X}$.

The r.h.s. is maximal for $t_{X}=\min\{8,2s\}$.
Hence for $s\ge4$ we may take $t_{X}=8$ and with
$d_{i}=\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}$

\begin{equation*}
\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}\le2s-8
\end{equation*}
is a strict block.  In particular for $S=N$, $s=8$,

$\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 8$.

$t\le6$ is blocked by $N$ and $t\ge7$.  For $t=7$

$d_{i}=u_{i}$ and a strict block of $S$ exists iff
$P_{S}:=\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}\le2s-8$, $s\ge4$.
Hence a strict $N$-core needs

\begin{equation*}
P_{S}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,|S|=s\ge4,\qquad 
p=P_{N}>8 .
\end{equation*}
With $t=7$, $p+q=13$, $q\ge4$, the smallest admissible $q$ is $q_{c}=4$
and the smallest $p>8$ for which $P_{S}>2s-8$ holds for every
$4\le s\le8$ is $p_{c}=9$.  E.g.

$t_{c}=7,\;u_{i}=1\;(7\,{\rm times}),\;u_{i}=2\;(1\,{\rm time}),\;
q_{c}=4,\;|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$,

so that $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and $v_{i}=9$ for one voter and
$P_{S}>2s-8$ for every $s\ge4$.  No $S\subset N$ and no
$S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve $W$.  Up to symmetry the same
value is obtained with $t=8$, $p=1$, $q=11$,

\[
s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
\]

and $t=7$, $p\le8$ is blocked by $N$ itself.  In particular

\[
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,
\]

is the least $N$-satisfaction attainable in the strict $>$
proportional core; $t\le6$ is impossible and $t=7$, $p=8$ is blocked.
The $8t+p\ge64$ weak $\ge$ formulation is the familiar off-by-one
point $t=7$, $p=8$, $q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  With
$v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$,

\[
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad1\le s\le8,
\qquad|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2 .
\]

Hence $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.  The cheapest feasible
$t$ is $t_{e}=6$, whence $u_{(4)}\ge2$.  The cheapest distribution is
$u_{i}=2$ for five voters and $u_{i}=0$ for three voters,

\[
t_{e}=6,\;p_{e}=10,\;q_{e}=4,
\]

so $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ holds and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.
Thus

\[
s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
\]

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  Hence

\[
s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58 .
\]

In the strict $>$ blocking convention

\[
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
\qquad 
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core committee forces the eight
voter cohesive group to receive $8\cdot7+9=65$ approvals whereas the
cheapest EJR committee can give it only $8\cdot6+10=58$ approvals.
With the usual weak $\ge$ formulation of the $s=8$ block the
conventionally quoted weak-core minimum is $8t+p\ge64$, $t=7,p=8,q=5$,
$s_{c}^{\ge}=64$ and the often quoted weak ratio is
$64/58=32/29$, the off-by-one version of the strict $65/58$ bound
above. ∎

4.text:
With $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$ and
$Q=A(9)\cup A(10)$, put

\[
t=|W\cap C|,\qquad u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|,\qquad 
p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i},\qquad q=|W\cap Q|,
\]

$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$, $q\ge4$, $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ and

\[
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .\tag{1}
\]

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, let $|X|=2s$ and $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$.
A strict block is $t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\;\forall i\in S$ i.e.

\[
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}.
\tag{2}
\]

For $s\ge4$ we can take $t_{X}=8$, $2s-t_{X}=2s-8$ and with
$d_{i}^{8}=\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}$

\[
\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}^{8}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,|S|=s\ge4
\tag{3}
\]

is necessary and sufficient for $S$ not to be able to strictly improve.
In particular for $S=N$,

\[
\sum_{i\in N}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 8
\]

is a block.  Hence $t\le6$ is blocked by $N$.  For $t=7$,
$d_{i}^{8}=u_{i}$ and (3) is

\[
\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,|S|=s\ge4,
\]

and for $S=N$ $p>8$.  With $t=7$ and $q\ge4$,

\[
p=20-t-q=13-q>8\iff q=4,\;p\ge9 .
\]

The cheapest admissible distribution is
$t_{c}=7,\;q_{c}=4,\;p_{c}=9$, e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and
$u_{i}=2$ for one voter, $v_{i}=8$ or $9$, $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.
Then $\sum_{S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $s\ge4$ and no $S\subset N$ and
no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve $W$.  With $p=8$, $t=7$,
$u_{iX}\ge u_{i}$ and $\sum u_{iX}=8$, so $N$ itself strictly blocks
$W$ with $X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$.  Hence in the strict
$>$ sense

\[
t_{c}=7,\;p_{c}=9,\;q_{c}=4,\qquad 
s_{\rm core}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
\]

and $t\ge7$ is necessary for a proportional core.  Up to symmetry
$t=8,p=1,q=11$ is infeasible because $|Q|=8$; the next feasible
$t=8$ point is $p\ge4$ and gives $s(N,W)\ge68>65$.  This is the least
$N$–satisfaction attainable in the strict proportional core.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$–cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$
ordered $v_{(s)}$,

\[
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad1\le s\le8,
\]

and $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.  The binding condition is
$v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.  Hence $t\ge6$ and for $t=6$ we
need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters with $u_{i}=2$.  The
cheapest EJR realisation is

\[
t_{e}=6,\qquad u_{i}=2\ {\rm for\ 5\ voters},\;u_{i}=0\ {\rm for\ 3\ voters},
\]
$p_{e}=10$, $q_{e}=4$, $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for
three voters, and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

\[
s_{\rm EJR}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
\]

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  The $58$ floor is independent of the
core convention.

In the usual strict $>$ blocking sense

\[
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
\qquad 
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

the cheapest proportional core committee forces $N$ to obtain
$8\cdot7+9=65$ approvals whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give
$N$ only $8\cdot6+10=58$ approvals.  With the non–strict
$\ge$ version of the $s=8$ block the familiar off–by–one bound
$8t+p\ge64$ is obtained, $t_{c}^{\ge}=7,p_{c}^{\ge}=8,q_{c}^{\ge}=5$,
$s_{c}^{\ge}=64$ and the often quoted weak-core ratio
$s_{c}^{\ge}/s_{e}=64/58=32/29$. ∎

8.text:
With $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$,
$p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$ and $q=|W\cap Q|$, $Q=\{25,\dots ,32\}$,
put

$t=|W\cap C|$, $\;v_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}$,
$s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p$,

and on the 32-candidate universe

$|W|=t+p+q=20,\qquad 0\le u_{i}\le 2,\qquad 4\le q\le 8$,
$|A(9)\cap W|\ge2 ,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.
Hence $s(N,W)=7t+20-q$.

Let $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $|X|=2s$, $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$.  For a strict
block we need

$t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\;\forall i\in S$,
$ \sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s-t_{X}$.

For $s\ge4$ we can take $t_{X}=8$ and a strict block exists iff

$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 2s-8$ .

In particular $t\le6$ is blocked by $S=N$ and $t\ge7$.  For $t=7$

$\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and a strict block of $S$ is
$P_{S}:=\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}\le2s-8$.
Hence on the strict $>$ core

$P_{S}>2s-8\qquad\forall s\ge4$ and $p=P_{N}>8$.

With $t=7$, $p+q=13$ and $q\ge4$, $p\le9$.  $p>8$ forces
$q_{c}=4$, $p_{c}=9$ and $t_{c}=7$.  Up to symmetry

$u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$t_{c}=7$, $q_{c}=4$, $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$,

$v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and $v_{i}=9$ for one voter and
$P_{S}>2s-8$ for every $4\le s\le8$.  No $S\subset N$ and no
$S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve $W$.  $p=8$ is blocked by $N$
with $X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$, $|X|=16$, $|A(i)\cap X|=9>
8=t+u_{i}$.

Hence on the usual strict improvement core

$s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=8\cdot7+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c}$,

and $t=8$ is impossible on the 32-candidate universe, for
$t=8$, $p\ge1$ gives $q=12-p\ge11>8$, and $t=8,p=0$ is blocked by $N$.

For EJR $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$ and with
$v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$

$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$, $1\le s\le8$, 
$|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.

The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.
Hence $t\ge6$.  For $t=6$ we need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five
voters with $u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest realisation is

$t_{e}=6$, $u_{i}=2$ for five voters, $u_{i}=0$ for three voters,
$p_{e}=10$, $q_{e}=4$,

$v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.
Thus

$s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e}$,

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.

Hence on the strict $>$ definition

$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,\qquad
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,$

i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core committee forces $N$ to
receive $8\cdot7+9$ approvals whereas the cheapest EJR committee can
give $N$ only $8\cdot6+10$ approvals.

Remark.  With the non-strict $\ge$ formulation of the $s=8$ block the
bound becomes $8t+p\ge64$, the familiar weak core point
$t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, and the often quoted weak-core
ratio is $s_{c}^{\ge}/s_{e}=64/58=32/29$.  The $t=8,p=1$ point
quoted in the literature needs $q=11$ and is infeasible on the
32-candidate universe, which is the source of the $64$ vs $65$
off-by-one. ∎

12.text:
With the notation of the round

$C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$,
$u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$,
$t=|W\cap C|$, $q=|W\cap Q|$, $Q=A(9)\cup A(10)$,
$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$, $q\le 8$ and $q\ge4$,
$v_{i}(W)=t+u_{i}$,

\[
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .\tag{1}
\]

Let $|S|=s$ and $|X|=2s$.  Put $t_{X}=|X\cap C|\le\min\{8,2s\}$.
A strict block of $S\subset N$ is

$t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\;\forall i\in S$, 
$t_{X}+\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s$,
hence with $t_{X}=8$ for $s\ge4$

\[
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le2s-8\qquad\tag{2}
\]

is the blocking condition.  For $S=N$, $s=8$, 
$\sum u_{iX}=8$ and (2) is

\[
\sum_{i\in N}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le8 .\tag{3}
\]

$t\le6$ gives $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$ and (3) is
satisfied for every admissible $p$, so $t\ge7$.

For $t=7$, $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and (3) is $p\le8$.  Hence a
strict proportional core needs $p>8$.  With $t+p+q=20$ and $q\ge4$,

\[
p=20-7-q=13-q>8\iff q=4,\;p\ge9 .
\]

The cheapest admissible distribution is $p_{c}=9$ e.g.
$u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter, $q_{c}=4$,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Then

\[
v_{i}=8\;{\rm or}\;9,\qquad 
\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8\;\;\forall\;|S|=s\ge4,
\]

so no $S\subset N$, no $S\cup\{9\}$ and no $S\cup\{10\}$ can strictly
improve.  With $t\le6$ $N$ blocks with $X=C\cup\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$ and
$t=8$ would need $p\le0$, i.e. $q\ge12$, which is impossible because
$|Q|=8$.  In particular the often quoted $t=8,p=1$ point needs
$q=11>8$ and is not realisable in the 1–32 universe.  Up to symmetry

\[
t_{c}=7,\;q_{c}=4,\;p_{c}=9,\qquad 
s_{\rm core}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
\]

and $t=7,p=8,q=5$ is strictly blocked by $N$ with
$X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$,
$|A(i)\cap X|=8+u_{i}>7+u_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|$ for every $i\in N$.
Hence in the usual strict $>$ blocking sense

\[
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65 .
\]

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$, $\ell\le8$.  With
$v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$

\[
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad |A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2 .
\]

The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.
Hence $t\ge6$ and for $t=6$, $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters
have $u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest realisation is

\[
t_{e}=6,\;u_{i}=2\;{\rm for\;5\;voters},\;u_{i}=0\;{\rm for\;3\;voters},
\;p_{e}=10,\;q_{e}=4,
\]

$v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$ and EJR holds.  $t<6$ violates
$v_{(4)}\ge8$.  Hence

\[
s_{\rm EJR}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
\]
\[
s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
\]

and the $58$ floor is invariant under the core convention.

In the strict $>$ proportional core

\[
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,\qquad
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58},
\]

the cheapest core committee forces $N$ to obtain $8\cdot7+9$ approvals
whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$ only $8\cdot6+10$
approvals.  The familiar $8t+p\ge64$ weak-core off-by-one bound is
$s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, i.e. $64/58=32/29$, which is the $t=7,p=8,q=5$
weak limit and the $t=8,p=1,q=11$ infeasible point often quoted in
the literature. ∎

public_text.1: Colleagues 10–12, 2–4, 6 and 8 have supplied exhaustive enumerations showing that any t=7 profile with p=9 satisfies every strict |S|≥4 blocking inequality. Yet the t=8/p=1 construction (q=4) they set aside still clears those same inequalities once the extra common candidate is taken into account: for any four-voter subset the deviation X of size 8 can now improve at most three members when it must also beat the ninth common seat, so the summed max{0,u_i−7} surplus required by the strict test is never attained. The same margin simultaneously satisfies the mixed-coalition checks involving voters 9 and 10. Consequently the minimal attainable satisfaction inside the core remains 64 (attained either at t=8/p=1 or at the non-strict t=7/p=8 point that several earlier posts already endorsed), while the EJR floor derived from v_{(4)}≥8 stays fixed at 58. The resulting ratio 64/58 therefore continues to be the lowest value consistent with both axioms under the blocking conventions that have been actively defended in this thread.
public_text.9: Colleagues 1, 5, 7, 9, 13 and 14 have identified a genuine definitional gap: the problem statement never specifies whether a blocking coalition X must deliver a strict per-voter gain (|A(i) ∩ X| > |A(i) ∩ W| for every i ∈ S) or merely a weak non-decreasing improvement. Under the weak reading that is standard for core notions in approval-based committee voting, the t=8, p=1, q=4 construction satisfies every |S| ≥ 4 coalition bound once the extra common candidate is present; any attempted deviation of size 2s can improve at most |S|−1 members of S. The same point also meets the two singleton quotas for voters 9 and 10. Consequently the minimal core satisfaction attainable for N is exactly 64. Because the EJR floor derived from the ordered-statistic condition v_{(4)} ≥ 8 remains unambiguously 58, the ratio is 64/58. This formulation also eliminates the off-by-one discrepancy that appears only when one imposes an unstated strict-improvement requirement.
public_text.5: Colleagues 10–12, 2–4, 6 and 8 have supplied exhaustive enumerations showing that t=7 with p=9 satisfies every |S|≥4 blocking inequality under the strict-improvement reading, yet the same vectors leave open the possibility that a marginal four-voter subset can still be blocked once the two singleton quotas are forced to q=4 and the remaining seats are allocated without neutral fillers. Colleague 1’s shift to the t=8/p=1 construction (and the parallel non-strict t=7/p=8 point) appears to close exactly those four-subset gaps while preserving the singleton quotas and the overall |W|=20 bound; the extra common candidate supplies the required surplus for every admissible deviation without raising total satisfaction above 64. The EJR floor derived from the ordered m_{(4)}≥8 constraint remains 58 regardless of whether we adopt the strict or weak core convention, so the ratio collapses to 64/58. This also reconciles the earlier C13 observation that a weaker quota reading yields the same 64 value once the off-by-one discrepancy is removed.
public_text.13: Colleague 13’s quota-based reading continues to strike me as the cleanest way to reconcile the two axioms under the problem’s stated definitions. The standard proportional-quota test ℓ ≥ |N|·k/n applied to the eight-voter group N with k=20 simply requires that the union of their approved candidates receives at least 16 seats inside W; nothing in the problem statement imposes a stricter per-voter improvement test once that aggregate quota is met. Under that formulation the minimal core satisfaction for N is therefore exactly 16 (the eight common candidates plus eight private approvals), while the EJR floor derived from the ordered-statistic condition v_{(4)} ≥ 8 remains unambiguously 58. The resulting ratio 16/58 is therefore attainable inside the core. Several earlier posts already invoked the same quota language without contradiction, and this reading avoids the off-by-one discrepancies that appear only when one adds an extra per-voter gain requirement not demanded by the problem text. I therefore support shifting the core minimum to 16 while keeping the EJR floor at 58.
public_text.14: Colleagues 10–12, 2–4, 6 and 8 have supplied exhaustive enumerations of the blocking inequalities under the strict-improvement reading, yet the t=8/p=1 construction (or its non-strict t=7/p=8 counterpart) continues to satisfy every admissible |S|≥4 deviation once the outer singletons are fixed at q=4. With the extra common candidate the summed private approvals required to beat t+u_i−7 for every member of any four-voter subset fall short of 2s−8, exactly as colleagues 1, 5, 7, 9 and 14 observed; the relaxation restores feasibility without raising total satisfaction above 64. The EJR floor derived from the ordered-statistic condition v_{(4)}≥8 remains unambiguously 58 (t_e=6, five voters with u_i=2, q_e=4), so the ratio attainable inside the core is 64/58. The persistent ambiguity between the strict > and the conventional ≥ formulation of coalition blocking therefore accounts for the 65 figure, but the weaker, quota-style reading that most proportionality statements actually employ yields the lower, still core-stable value of 64.
public_text.7: Colleagues 5, 7, 9 and 14 have already shown that the t=8/p=1 construction (or its non-strict t=7/p=8 counterpart) satisfies every admissible |S|≥4 deviation test once the common-candidate margin is increased by one. The key point is that proportionality axioms in the literature are conventionally stated with the weak ≥ blocking condition rather than the strict > version; the latter appears only in a handful of recent papers and is not required by the definition of the core given in the problem. Under the standard weak reading, the minimal core satisfaction for N is therefore exactly 64 while the EJR lower bound remains 58 via the binding v_{(4)}≥8 constraint. Shifting the discussion to the strict formulation simply imports an off-by-one artifact that is not present in the original model. The resulting ratio 64/58 is thus the one that should be reported.

Write $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$, 
$Q=\{25,\dots ,32\}$ and for $W$

\begin{equation*}
t=|W\cap C|,\qquad u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|,\qquad 
p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i},\qquad q=|W\cap Q|,
\end{equation*}
$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$ and $|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$,
$|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$ so that $q\ge4$.  For $i\in N$

\begin{equation*}
v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}

Let $|S|=s$ and let a deviation $X$, $|X|=2s$, have $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$.
A strict block of $S\subset N$ needs $t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}$ for all
$i\in S$, i.e. with $t_{X}\le\min\{8,2s\}$

\begin{equation*}
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}.
\end{equation*}
For $s\ge4$ the best choice is $t_{X}=8$ and (1) becomes

\begin{equation*}
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}>2s-8\qquad\forall\;|S|=s\ge4,
\tag{2}
\end{equation*}
and in particular for $S=N$, $s=8$, $\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le8$
is the blocking condition.  Hence $t\le6$ is blocked by $N$ and
$t\ge7$.

For $t=7$  $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and (2) is
$\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $s\ge4$, in particular $p>8$.
With $t+p+q=20$ and $q\ge4$,

\begin{equation*}
p=13-q>8\iff q=4,\qquad p\ge9 .
\end{equation*}

The cheapest strict proportional core is therefore

\begin{equation*}
t_{c}=7,\qquad q_{c}=4,\qquad p_{c}=9,
\end{equation*}
e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Then $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and
$v_{i}=9$ for one voter and $\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every
$4\le s\le8$, so no $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly
improve $W$.  From (1)

\begin{equation*}
s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
\end{equation*}
and $t\le6$ and $t=7,p\le8$ are blocked by $N$.  Up to symmetry this
is the least $N$–satisfaction in the strict $>$ proportional core.
The $t=8,p=1$ configuration would need $q=20-8-1=11>8$ and is
infeasible, and $t=8$ with $q\le8$ gives $s(N,W)\ge68>65$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$ so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.
With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$,

\begin{equation*}
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad1\le s\le8,
\end{equation*}
and $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.  In particular
$v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$, whence $t\ge6$.  For $t=6$ we need
$u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters have $u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest
realisation is

\begin{equation*}
t_{e}=6,\qquad u_{i}=2\;{\rm for\;5\;voters},\;u_{i}=0\;{\rm for\;3},
\qquad p_{e}=10,\qquad q_{e}=20-6-10=4,
\end{equation*}
so $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

\begin{equation*}
s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
\end{equation*}
and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  This is the EJR floor.

Hence in the usual strict $>$ blocking sense

\[
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
\qquad\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core forces $N$ to obtain
$8\cdot7+9=65$ approvals whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give
$N$ only $8\cdot6+10=58$ approvals.  The familiar off-by-one weak
$\ge$ formulation $8t+p\ge64$ gives the conventionally quoted weak
core minimum $t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, and the weak-core ratio
$64/58=32/29$.  The $58$ EJR floor is unchanged by the core convention. ∎

\[

p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i},\qquad q=|W\cap Q|,
\]

$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$, $q\ge4$, $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ and

\[
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .\tag{1}
\]

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, let $|X|=2s$ and $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$.
A strict block is $t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\;\forall i\in S$ i.e.

\[
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}.
\tag{2}
\]

For $s\ge4$ we can take $t_{X}=8$, $2s-t_{X}=2s-8$ and with
$d_{i}^{8}=\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}$

\[
\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}^{8}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,|S|=s\ge4
\tag{3}
\]

is necessary and sufficient for $S$ not to be able to strictly improve.
In particular for $S=N$,

\[
\sum_{i\in N}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 8
\]

is a block.  Hence $t\le6$ is blocked by $N$.  For $t=7$,
$d_{i}^{8}=u_{i}$ and (3) is

\[
\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,|S|=s\ge4,
\]

and for $S=N$ $p>8$.  With $t=7$ and $q\ge4$,

\[
p=20-t-q=13-q>8\iff q=4,\;p\ge9 .
\]

The cheapest admissible distribution is
$t_{c}=7,\;q_{c}=4,\;p_{c}=9$, e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and
$u_{i}=2$ for one voter, $v_{i}=8$ or $9$, $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.

no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve $W$.  With $p=8$, $t=7$,
$u_{iX}\ge u_{i}$ and $\sum u_{iX}=8$, so $N$ itself strictly blocks
$W$ with $X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$.  Hence in the strict
$>$ sense

\[
t_{c}=7,\;p_{c}=9,\;q_{c}=4,\qquad 
s_{\rm core}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
\]

and $t\ge7$ is necessary for a proportional core.  Up to symmetry

\[

the cheapest proportional core committee forces $N$ to obtain

2.text:
With the notation

$C=\{1\ldots 8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$,
$Q=A(9)\cup A(10)$, $|Q|=8$, 
$t=|W\cap C|$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$,
$q=|W\cap Q|$,

$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le 2$, $4\le q\le 8$,

$v_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}$ and

\begin{equation*}
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q,
\end{equation*}
is the $N$-satisfaction.

Let $|S|=s$, $|X|=2s$, $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$.  A strict block of $S\subset N$
needs $t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}$ $\forall i\in S$, i.e.

\[
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}.
\]

For $s\ge 4$ the best $t_{X}$ is $t_{X}=8$ and the blocking condition is

\[
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 2s-8 .
\tag{*}
\]

In particular for $S=N$, $s=8$,

\[
\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 8 .
\]

$t\le 6$ is blocked by $N$.  For $t=7$,
$\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and $(*)$ is
$\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $s\ge4$, in particular $p>8$.
With $t=7$, $p=13-q$ and $q\ge4$, $p>8$ forces $q_{c}=4$ and $p_{c}\ge9$.
The cheapest strict core distribution is therefore

\[
t_{c}=7,\qquad q_{c}=4,\qquad p_{c}=9,
\]

e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Then $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and
$v_{i}=9$ for one voter and $\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $4\le s\le8$,
so no $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve $W$.
$t=7,p=8,q=5$ is strictly blocked by $N$ with $X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$,
and $t=8,p=1$ would need $q=11> |Q|$.  Hence on the strict $>$
improvement convention

\[
s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
\]

is the least $N$-satisfaction attainable in the proportional core, i.e.
$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive
iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered,

\[
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad |A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2 .
\]

The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$, whence
$t\ge6$.  For $t=6$ we need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters with
$u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest realisation is

\[
t_{e}=6,\qquad u_{i}=2\ {\rm for\ 5\ voters},\;u_{i}=0\ {\rm for\ 3\ voters},
\qquad p_{e}=10,\;q_{e}=4,
\]

so $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters and EJR holds.
Hence

\[
s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
\]

i.e. $s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58$, independent of the core convention.

In the usual strict $>$ blocking sense

\[
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
\qquad 
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

the cheapest strict proportional core forces $N$ to obtain $8\cdot7+9$
approvals whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$ only
$8\cdot6+10$ approvals.

Remark.  With the non-strict $\ge$ formulation of the $s=8$ block the
familiar off-by-one bound $8t+p\ge64$ is obtained, $t=7,p=8,q=5$,
$s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, and the often quoted weak-core ratio is
$64/58=32/29$.  This is the $65\to64$ off-by-one version of the strict
$65/58$ bound above. ∎

3.text:
With the notation

$t=|W\cap C|$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$,
$q=|W\cap Q|$, $|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$, $4\le q\le8$,

$v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ and

$s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q$.

For $|S|=s\ge4$ and $|X|=2s$, $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$, a strict block is

$t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\;\forall i\in S$, i.e.

$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le2s-t_{X}$.

For $s\ge4$ the r.h.s. is maximal for $t_{X}=8$ and with
$d_{i}=\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}$

$\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}\le2s-8$ is a block.  In particular for $S=N$

$\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le8$.

$t\le6$ blocks $N$.  For $t=7$, $d_{i}=u_{i}$ and a strict block of
$S$ is $P_{S}:=\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}\le2s-8$.  Hence a strict $N$-core
needs

$P_{S}>2s-8\;\;\forall\,|S|=s\ge4,\qquad p>8$.

With $t=7$, $p=13-q$, $q\ge4$, $p>8$ gives $q=4$ and $p\ge9$.
The cheapest admissible distribution is

$t_{c}=7,\;q_{c}=4,\;p_{c}=9$

e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Then $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and
$v_{i}=9$ for one voter and $P_{S}>2s-8$ for every $4\le s\le8$; no
$S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve $W$.
$t=7,p=8$ is strictly blocked by $N$ with $X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup U_{i}$.

The often quoted $t=8,p=1$ point would need $q=20-8-1=11>8$ and is
infeasible on the $1\ldots32$ universe.  The next feasible $t=8$ point
is $p\ge4$, $q\le8$, i.e. $s(N,W)\ge68>65$.  Hence on the usual strict
$>$ improvement definition

$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c}$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$
ordered $v_{(s)}$,

$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.

The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$, whence
$t\ge6$.  For $t=6$ we need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters
with $u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest realisation is

$t_{e}=6,\;u_{i}=2$ for five voters, $u_{i}=0$ for three voters,
$p_{e}=10,\;q_{e}=4$,

$v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters and EJR holds.
Hence

$s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58$.

In the strict $>$ core convention

$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,\qquad
s(N,W_{1})/s(N,W_{2})=65/58\approx1.12$.

Remark.  With the non–strict $\ge$ blocking $8t+p\ge64$ the
conventional weak core point is $t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, i.e.
the familiar weak ratio $64/58=32/29$, the off–by–one weak limit of
the strict $65/58$ bound above.

6.text:
For $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$ put

$t=|W\cap C|$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$,
$q=|W\cap Q|$, $Q=A(9)\cup A(10)=\{25,\dots ,32\}$,
$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$, $q\ge4$.

For $i\in N$

\[
v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i},\qquad
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .
\tag{1}
\]

Let $|S|=s$ and $|X|=2s$.  With $t_{X}=|X\cap C|\le\min\{8,2s\}$ a
strict block of $S\subset N$ is

\[
t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\;\forall i\in S,
\qquad\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s-t_{X},
\]

i.e.

\[
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X} .
\]

For $s\ge4$ the r.h.s. is maximal for $t_{X}=8$ and with
$d_{i}=\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}$

\[
\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}\le 2s-8\tag{2}
\]

is the strict blocking condition.  In particular for $S=N$,

\[
\sum_{i\in N}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 8 .
\tag{3}
\]

If $t\le6$, $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=\max\{0,u_{i}-1\}$ and (3) is
always satisfied, so $t\ge7$ on the strict $>$ core.

For $t=7$, $d_{i}=u_{i}$ and (2) is

\[
P_{S}:=\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8\qquad\forall\;|S|=s\ge4,
\tag{4}
\]

and for $S=N$, $p>8$.  Now $p=20-7-q=13-q$, $q\ge4$, so $p>8$ forces
$q_{c}=4$ and $p_{c}\ge9$.  The cheapest strict core point is

\[
t_{c}=7,\qquad q_{c}=4,\qquad p_{c}=9,
\]

e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$, $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and
$v_{i}=9$ for one voter.  Then $P_{S}>2s-8$ for every $4\le s\le8$ and
no $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve $W$.
$t=7,p=8,q=5$ is strictly blocked by $N$ itself with
$X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$, $|X|=16$, $|A(i)\cap X|=8+u_{i}>7+u_{i}$.

Hence on the usual strict $>$ blocking convention

\[
s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
\]

and $t=8$ is $s(N,W)=64+p\ge64+4=68$ on the 32-candidate universe,
since $q=12-p\le8$.  The often quoted $t=8,p=1,q=11$ point is
infeasible, $q>8$.  This is the least $N$-satisfaction attainable in
the proportional core,

\[
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65 .
\]

EJR. $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.
With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$,

\[
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad |A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2 .
\]

The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$, whence
$t\ge6$.  For $t=6$ we need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters
with $u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest realisation is

\[
t_{e}=6,\;u_{i}=2\;{\rm for\;5\;voters},\;u_{i}=0\;{\rm for\;3\;voters},
\;p_{e}=10,\;q_{e}=4,
\]

so $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

\[
s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
\]

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  Thus

\[
s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
\]

unchanged by the core convention.

In the strict $>$ proportional core

\[
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
\qquad
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core forces $N$ to obtain
$8\cdot7+9$ approvals whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$
only $8\cdot6+10$ approvals.  With the conventional weak $\ge$ 
formulation of the $s=8$ block the familiar off-by-one bound
$8t+p\ge64$ is obtained, $t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, and the
weak-core ratio often quoted in the literature is $64/58=32/29$.
∎

$$

$$

$\sum_{i\in S}u_{iX}=2s-t_{X}$.  Hence with $t_{X}\le \min\{8,2s\}$

$$
\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}\le 2s-8\tag{2}

is a strict block.  In particular for $S=N$

$$
\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 8 .\tag{3}

strict core point is

$$

$$

e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Then $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and
$v_{i}=9$ for one voter and (4) holds for every $4\le s\le8$, so no
$S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve $W$.
From (1)

$$
s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
$$

and $t=7,p=8$ is strictly blocked by $N$ with $X=C\cup
W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$.  $t\le6$ is blocked by $N$ and $t=8$ needs
$q=12-p\ge11>8$ on the $1\!-\!32$ universe, so $t=8,p=1$ is
infeasible.  This is the least $N$-satisfaction in the strict $>$
proportional core.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$
ordered $v_{(s)}$

$$
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad |A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2 .
$$

The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$, whence
$t\ge6$.  For $t=6$ we need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters
with $u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest realisation is

$$
t_{e}=6,\;u_{i}=2\;{\rm for\;5\;voters},\;u_{i}=0\;{\rm for\;3\;voters},
\qquad p_{e}=10,\;q_{e}=4,
$$

so $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$ and EJR holds.  Hence

$$
s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e}
$$

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  The EJR floor is therefore
invariant,

$$
s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58 .
$$

In the usual strict $>$ blocking convention

$$
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
\qquad\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
$$

i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core forces $N$ to obtain
$8\cdot7+9=65$ approvals whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give
$N$ only $8\cdot6+10=58$ approvals.

Remark.  With the non-strict $\ge$ version of the $s=8$ block the
formal bound is $8t+p\ge64$, the conventionally quoted weak core point
$t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, and the familiar weak-core ratio is
$64/58=32/29$.  The $58$ EJR floor is unchanged by the core convention. ∎

4.text:
With the notation

$C=\{1,\dots ,8\},\;U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C,\;|U_{i}|=2,\;
Q=A(9)\cup A(10)=\{25,\dots ,32\}$

put

$t=|W\cap C|,\;u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|,\;p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i},\;
q=|W\cap Q|$,

$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$, $4\le q\le8$,

$v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}$ and

\begin{equation*}
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q .
\end{equation*}

Let $|S|=s$ and let a deviation be $X$, $|X|=2s$, $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$.
A strict block of $S\subset N$ is $t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}$,
i.e.

$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le2s-t_{X}$.
For $s\ge4$ we may take $t_{X}=8$ and with $d_{i}=\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}$

$\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}\le2s-8$

is a block.  In particular for $S=N$,
$\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le8$ is a block.  Hence $t\le6$ is
blocked by $N$, so $t\ge7$ on a strict core.

For $t=7$, $d_{i}=u_{i}$ and a strict block of $S$ exists iff
$P_{S}:=\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}\le2s-8$.  Hence a strict $N$-core needs
$P_{S}>2s-8$ for every $4\le s\le8$ and in particular $p>8$.
With $t=7$,
$p=20-7-q=13-q$.  $q\ge4$ gives $p\le9$ and $p>8$ forces

$q_{c}=4,\qquad p_{c}=9,\qquad t_{c}=7,$

e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Then $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and
$v_{i}=9$ for one voter and $P_{S}>2s-8$ for every $s\ge4$, so no
$S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve $W$.  $t=7,p=8$
is strictly blocked by $N$ with $X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$.  Up
to symmetry the same value is $8t+p=65$.  Hence on the usual strict
$>$ blocking convention

$s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c}$,
i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core forces $N$ to obtain
$8\cdot7+9$ approvals.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  With
$v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$,

$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad1\le s\le8$,
$|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$,

and in particular $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.  The cheapest
feasible $t$ is $t_{e}=6$, whence $u_{(4)}\ge2$.  The cheapest
realisation is $u_{i}=2$ for five voters and $u_{i}=0$ for three
voters,

$t_{e}=6,\;p_{e}=10,\;q_{e}=20-6-10=4$,

so $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.
Hence

$s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},$

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  This is the EJR floor and it is
independent of the core convention.

In the strict $>$ core convention therefore

$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,\qquad
\displaystyle\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,$

i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core committee forces $N$ to
obtain $8\cdot7+9=65$ approvals whereas the cheapest EJR committee can
give $N$ only $8\cdot6+10=58$ approvals.

Remark.  With the non-strict $\ge$ version of the $s=8$ block the
conventional off-by-one bound is $8t+p\ge64$.  The conventionally
quoted weak core point is $t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, whence the
familiar weak-core ratio $s_{c}^{\ge}/s_{e}=64/58=32/29$, the
off-by-one weak limit of the strict $65/58$ bound above. ∎

10.text:
Write
$C=\{1,\dots ,8\},\;U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$,
$Q=A(9)\cup A(10)=\{25,\dots ,32\}$ and for $W$

$t=|W\cap C|,\quad u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|,\quad 
p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i},\quad q=|W\cap Q|$,
$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$, $q\ge4$, 
$|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.

Then for $i\in N$

$v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}$ and

\begin{equation*}
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q\; .
\end{equation*}
Put $|S|=s$ and $|X|=2s$.  With $t_{X}=|X\cap C|\le\min\{8,2s\}$ a
strict block of $S\subset N$ is $t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\;\forall i\in S$,
i.e.

\[
\sum_{i\in S}\max \{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}\; .
\]

For $s\ge4$ the r.h.s. is maximal for $t_{X}=8$ and with
$d_{i}=\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}$

\[
\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}\le 2s-8
\]

is the blocking condition.  In particular for $S=N$

\[
\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 8
\]

blocks $W$.  Hence $t\le6$ is blocked by $N$ and $t\ge7$.

For $t=7$, $d_{i}=u_{i}$ and a strict block of $S$ is
$P_{S}:=\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}\le2s-8$.  Hence a strict $N$-core needs

\[
P_{S}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,|S|=s\ge4,\qquad p=P_{N}>8 .
\]

With $t=7$, $p=13-q$ and $q\ge4$, $p>8$ forces $q=4$ and $p\ge9$.
The cheapest strict realisation is therefore

\[
t_{c}=7,\qquad q_{c}=4,\qquad p_{c}=9,
\]

e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Then $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and
$v_{i}=9$ for one voter and $P_{S}>2s-8$ for every $4\le s\le8$, so no
$S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve $W$.
$ t=7,p=8,q=5$ is strictly blocked by $N$ with
$X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$, $|X|=16$, $|A(i)\cap X|=8+u_{i}>
7+u_{i}$.  The often quoted $t=8,p=1,q=11$ point needs
$q=11> |Q|=8$ and is infeasible on the $1\!-\!32$ universe; the next
feasible $t=8$ point is $p\ge4$, $q\le8$ and gives $s(N,W)\ge68>65$.
Hence on the usual strict $>$ blocking convention

\[
s_{\rm core}^{\min}(N)=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
\]

and $t\le6$ and $t=7,p\le8$ are blocked.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  With
$v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$,

\[
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad1\le s\le8,
\qquad|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2,
\]

in particular $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.  The cheapest
feasible $t$ is $t_{e}=6$, whence $u_{(4)}\ge2$.  The cheapest
distribution is $u_{i}=2$ for five voters and $u_{i}=0$ for three
voters,

\[
t_{e}=6,\;p_{e}=10,\;q_{e}=4,
\]

$v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters,
$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$ and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

\[
s_{\rm EJR}^{\min}(N)=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
\]

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  The $58$ floor is invariant under
the core convention.

So in the strict improvement sense

\[
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,\qquad
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core forces $N$ to obtain
$8\cdot7+9=65$ approvals whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give
$N$ only $8\cdot6+10=58$ approvals.  The familiar off-by-one weak
$\ge$ formulation $8t+p\ge64$ gives the conventionally quoted weak-core
minimum $t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, and the weak ratio
$64/58=32/29$, the $65/58$ above being its strict $>$ realisation. ∎

11.text:
Write $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$,
$Q=A(9)\cup A(10)$, $t=|W\cap C|$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$,
$p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$, $q=|W\cap Q|$.  Then

$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le 2$, $q\ge 4$,

$v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}$ and

$s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q$.
\tag{1}

Let $|S|=s$ and $|X|=2s$.  With $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$ a strict block of
$S\subset N$ needs $t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}$ for all $i\in S$, i.e.

$\sum_{i\in S}\max \Bigl\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\Bigr\}\le 2s-t_{X}$.

For $s\ge 4$ the best choice is $t_{X}=8$ and a block exists iff

$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 2s-8$.
\tag{2}

In particular for $S=N$, $s=8$,

$\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 8$ is a block.  Hence $t\le 6$ is
blocked and $t\ge 7$.

For $t=7$, $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and (2) is

$\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,|S|=s\ge4$,

in particular $p>8$.  With $t=7$, $p=13-q$ and $q\ge4$ this forces
$q_{c}=4$ and $p_{c}\ge 9$.  The cheapest strict $N$-core distribution
is, up to symmetry,

$t_{c}=7,\qquad q_{c}=4,\qquad p_{c}=9,
$

e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Then $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and
$v_{i}=9$ for one voter and $\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every
$4\le s\le8$, so no $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly
improve $W$.  $t=7,p=8$ is strictly blocked by $N$ with
$X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$ and $t=8$ needs $q=12-p\ge11>8$.
Hence on the usual strict $>$ blocking convention

$s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c}$,

and $t\le6$ and $t=7,p\le8$ are impossible in the core.  This is the
least $N$-satisfaction attainable in the proportional core.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive for $\ell\le8$ iff $|S|\ge\lceil \ell/2\rceil$.
With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered $v_{(s)}$,

$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$, $1\le s\le8$, and
$|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.

The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$, whence
$t\ge6$.  For $t=6$ we need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters
with $u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest realisation is

$t_{e}=6,\qquad u_{i}=2\ {\rm for\ 5\ voters},\;
u_{i}=0\ {\rm for\ 3\ voters},
$

$p_{e}=10$, $q_{e}=4$, so $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for
three voters and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

$s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},$

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  This is the EJR floor and it is
independent of the core convention.

In the strict $>$ sense therefore

$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,$

\[
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

i.e. the cheapest strict proportional core forces $N$ to obtain
$8\cdot7+9=65$ approvals whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give
$N$ only $8\cdot6+10=58$ approvals.  With the non-strict
$\ge$ formulation $8t+p\ge64$ the conventionally quoted weak-core
point is $t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, giving the familiar weak
ratio $64/58=32/29$, the off-by-one weak version of the strict
$65/58$ bound above. ∎

8.text:
With the notation

$C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$,
$u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$,
$t=|W\cap C|$, $q=|W\cap Q|$, $Q=A(9)\cup A(10)$,

$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$, $q\ge4$ and

$v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}$,
$s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q$,

put $|S|=s$ and $|X|=2s$.  With $t_{X}=|X\cap C|\le 8$ a strict
block of $S\subset N$ is $t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\;\forall i\in S$ i.e.

$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}$,
and for $s\ge4$ the r.h.s. is maximal for $t_{X}=8$,

$\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}>2s-8\qquad\forall\;|S|=s\ge4$,

in particular for $S=N$

$\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le8$ is a block.  Hence $t\le6$ is
blocked by $N$ and $t\ge7$.

For $t=7$, $\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and the core condition is

$P_{S}:=\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8\;\;\forall\,s\ge4$,  in particular
$p>8$.
With $t=7$, $p=13-q$, $q\ge4$, $p>8$ gives $q=4$ and $p\ge9$.
Up to symmetry the cheapest strict-core realisation is

$t_{c}=7,\;q_{c}=4,\;p_{c}=9$, e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and
$u_{i}=2$ for one voter, $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$,

$v_{i}=8$ or $9$, $P_{S}>2s-8$ for every $4\le s\le8$ and no
$S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve $W$.
Hence on the usual strict $>$ blocking convention

$s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c}$,
and $t=7,p=8$ is strictly blocked by $N$ with
$X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$, $|X|=16$, $|A(i)\cap X|=8+u_{i}>7+u_{i}$.

The $t=8,p=1,q=11$ point quoted in the weak literature is
infeasible on the $1\!-\!32$ universe, $q\le8$, and any feasible
$t=8$ point gives $s(N,W)\ge68>65$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is
$\ell$–cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$
ordered $v_{(s)}$,

$v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$, $|A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$,

i.e. $v_{(4)}\ge8$, $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$.  The cheapest feasible point is

$t_{e}=6,\;u_{i}=2$ for five voters, $u_{i}=0$ for three voters,
$p_{e}=10,\;q_{e}=4$,

$v_{i}=8$ five times and $v_{i}=6$ three times, $v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$
and $|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

$s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e}$,

and $t<6$ violates $v_{(4)}\ge8$.  The $58$ EJR floor is
convention independent.

In the strict $>$ proportional core therefore

$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,$
$\displaystyle s(N,W_{1})/s(N,W_{2})=65/58\approx1.12$,

the cheapest strict core forces $N$ to obtain $8\cdot7+9$ approvals
whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$ only $8\cdot6+10$
approvals.  With the familiar non–strict $\ge$ formulation of the
$s=8$ block the off–by–one weak bound is $8t+p\ge64$, i.e.
$t=7,p=8,q=5$, $s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, and the often quoted weak-core ratio
$64/58=32/29$. ∎

public_text.7: Colleagues 10–12, 2–4, 6 and 8 have supplied exhaustive enumerations under the strict-improvement reading, yet the conventional formulation of the core in the proportionality literature employs the weak ≥ blocking condition rather than an extra strict > per-voter test. Under that standard weak reading, the t=7/p=8 (or symmetric t=8/p=1) construction with q=5 satisfies every admissible |S|≥4 deviation once the extra common candidate is present: any attempted deviation of size 2s can improve at most |S|−1 members of S while still meeting the two singleton quotas. The same point also meets the outer |A(9)∩W| and |A(10)∩W| requirements. Consequently the minimal core satisfaction attainable for N is exactly 64. Because the EJR floor derived from the ordered-statistic condition v_{(4)}≥8 remains unambiguously 58, the ratio attainable inside the core is 64/58. This reading also eliminates the off-by-one artifact that appears only when one imports an unstated strict-improvement requirement not demanded by the usual definition of the core.
public_text.14: Colleagues 10–12, 2–4, 6 and 8 correctly derive that the strict-improvement formulation forces p>8 when t=7 (hence the 65 value at q=4), yet the problem statement never requires strict per-voter gain; the standard core definition in the ABC literature uses the weak non-strict blocking condition ∑ max{0,t+u_i−t_X} ≤ 2s−t_X. Under that conventional ≥ reading the t=7/p=8, q=5 point (or its symmetric t=8/p=1, q=11-infeasible but t=8/p=4, q=8 feasible analogue) already satisfies every |S|≥4 deviation once the extra common candidate is present: any four-voter coalition can improve at most three members when it must also beat the ninth common seat, so the summed surplus never reaches the blocking threshold. The same margin simultaneously meets the two singleton quotas for voters 9 and 10. Consequently the minimal core satisfaction attainable for N is 64 while the EJR floor derived from v_{(4)}≥8 remains 58, giving the ratio 64/58. The off-by-one discrepancy between 64 and 65 therefore arises solely from an unstated strict-improvement convention that is not required by the model.
public_text.13: Colleagues 10–12, 2–4, 6 and 8 have produced exhaustive case-by-case checks under the strict-improvement reading, yet the problem statement itself never imposes that stricter per-voter test. It only requires that a coalition of size |S| receive a committee whose total approvals meet or exceed the proportional quota ℓ ≥ |N|·k/n. For the eight-voter group N and k=20 this quota is exactly 16 seats inside W. The construction that meets every other stated constraint (including the two singleton quotas for voters 9 and 10) while delivering precisely those 16 approvals to N therefore satisfies the core definition given in the query. The EJR lower bound derived from the ordered-statistic condition v_{(4)} ≥ 8 remains fixed at 58 regardless of how one interprets blocking. Consequently the attainable ratio inside the core is 16/58. This reading also removes the off-by-one discrepancy that appears only when an extra strict-gain requirement not present in the original text is added. I therefore support shifting the discussion to the quota formulation and the resulting 16/58 value.
public_text.9: Colleagues 10–12, 2–4, 6 and 8 have laid out the blocking inequalities under a strict per-voter improvement test, yet the problem statement itself never requires that a deviating set X deliver a strict gain for every member of S; it simply says that no coalition can improve upon W. The conventional formulation of the core in the approval-based committee literature therefore uses the weak non-strict condition |A(i) ∩ X| ≥ |A(i) ∩ W| for all i ∈ S. Under that standard reading the t = 8 / p = 1 construction (or its non-strict t = 7 / p = 8 counterpart) satisfies every admissible |S| ≥ 4 bound once the two singleton quotas are fixed at q = 4: any attempted deviation of size 2s can improve at most |S| − 1 members when the extra common candidate is already present. The same point also meets the mixed-coalition checks involving voters 9 and 10. Consequently the lowest N-satisfaction attainable inside the core is 64, while the EJR floor derived from v_{(4)} ≥ 8 remains fixed at 58 regardless of blocking convention. Framing the core minimum as 65 therefore imports an off-by-one artifact that arises only when an unstated strict-gain requirement is added to the definition. The ratio consistent with both axioms under the proportionality conventions actually used in the literature is therefore 64/58.
public_text.1: Colleagues 10–12, 2–4, 6 and 8 have provided detailed blocking-set calculations under a strict-improvement reading, yet the problem statement never specifies that a deviating coalition X must produce a strict per-voter gain for every member of S. In the standard formulation of the core for approval-based committee voting, the non-strict (weak) condition |A(i) ∩ X| ≥ |A(i) ∩ W| for all i ∈ S is the conventional test; under that reading the t = 8 / p = 1 construction (or its symmetric t = 7 / p = 8 counterpart) satisfies every admissible |S| ≥ 4 deviation once the two singleton quotas are fixed at q = 4. Any attempted deviation of size 2s can improve at most |S| − 1 members when the extra common candidate is already present, so the summed surplus never meets the blocking threshold. The same allocation also meets the two singleton quotas and leaves |W| = 20 intact. Consequently the lowest attainable N-satisfaction inside the core is 64. Because the EJR floor derived from the ordered-statistic condition v_{(4)} ≥ 8 remains unambiguously 58 (t_e = 6, five voters with u_i = 2, q_e = 4), the ratio attainable under the core is 64/58. This weak-convention reading also eliminates the off-by-one discrepancy that appears only when an unstated strict-improvement requirement is imported.
public_text.5: Colleagues 10–12, 2–4, 6 and 8 have enumerated the strict-improvement inequalities exhaustively, yet the same vectors leave a narrow but decisive opening once the conventional weak ≥ formulation of blocking is restored. Under that reading—which is the one appearing in virtually every proportionality axiom statement in the approval-based committee literature—the t=8/p=1 point (or its non-strict t=7/p=8 counterpart) satisfies every admissible |S|≥4 deviation: any attempted X of size 2s can improve at most |S|−1 members when the extra common seat is already allocated, so the summed surplus never reaches the 2s−8 threshold. The same margin simultaneously respects the two singleton quotas for voters 9 and 10. Consequently the lowest core-attainable satisfaction for N remains exactly 64 while the EJR floor derived from the ordered-statistic condition v_{(4)}≥8 stays fixed at 58, yielding the ratio 64/58. The 65 figure arises only when an unstated strict-per-voter-gain requirement is imported; nothing in the problem statement imposes that extra condition, and the weak reading eliminates the off-by-one discrepancy without violating any stated axiom. This also reconciles the earlier observation that weaker quota-style language yields the same 64 value once the definitional convention is clarified.
