With the notation

$C=\{1\ldots 8\}$, $U_{i}=A(i)\setminus C$, $|U_{i}|=2$,
$Q=A(9)\cup A(10)$, $|Q|=8$, 
$t=|W\cap C|$, $u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|$, $p=\sum_{i\in N}u_{i}$,
$q=|W\cap Q|$,

$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le 2$, $4\le q\le 8$,

$v_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}$ and

\begin{equation*}
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q,
\end{equation*}
is the $N$-satisfaction.

Let $|S|=s$, $|X|=2s$, $t_{X}=|X\cap C|$.  A strict block of $S\subset N$
needs $t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}$ $\forall i\in S$, i.e.

\[
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}.
\]

For $s\ge 4$ the best $t_{X}$ is $t_{X}=8$ and the blocking condition is

\[
\sum_{i\in S}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 2s-8 .
\tag{*}
\]

In particular for $S=N$, $s=8$,

\[
\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 8 .
\]

$t\le 6$ is blocked by $N$.  For $t=7$,
$\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}=u_{i}$ and $(*)$ is
$\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $s\ge4$, in particular $p>8$.
With $t=7$, $p=13-q$ and $q\ge4$, $p>8$ forces $q_{c}=4$ and $p_{c}\ge9$.
The cheapest strict core distribution is therefore

\[
t_{c}=7,\qquad q_{c}=4,\qquad p_{c}=9,
\]

e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Then $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and
$v_{i}=9$ for one voter and $\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}>2s-8$ for every $4\le s\le8$,
so no $S\subset N$ and no $S\cup\{9,10\}$ can strictly improve $W$.
$t=7,p=8,q=5$ is strictly blocked by $N$ with $X=C\cup W\cap\bigcup_{i}U_{i}$,
and $t=8,p=1$ would need $q=11> |Q|$.  Hence on the strict $>$
improvement convention

\[
s_{c}^{\min}=8t_{c}+p_{c}=56+9=65=7t_{c}+20-q_{c},
\]

is the least $N$-satisfaction attainable in the proportional core, i.e.
$s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive
iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  With $v_{i}=t+u_{i}$ ordered,

\[
v_{(s)}\ge\min\{8,2s\},\qquad |A(9)\cap W|,|A(10)\cap W|\ge2 .
\]

The binding condition is $v_{(4)}\ge8$, i.e. $t+u_{(4)}\ge8$, whence
$t\ge6$.  For $t=6$ we need $u_{(4)}\ge2$, i.e. at least five voters with
$u_{i}=2$.  The cheapest realisation is

\[
t_{e}=6,\qquad u_{i}=2\ {\rm for\ 5\ voters},\;u_{i}=0\ {\rm for\ 3\ voters},
\qquad p_{e}=10,\;q_{e}=4,
\]

so $v_{i}=8$ for five voters and $v_{i}=6$ for three voters and EJR holds.
Hence

\[
s_{e}^{\min}=8t_{e}+p_{e}=48+10=58=7t_{e}+20-q_{e},
\]

i.e. $s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58$, independent of the core convention.

In the usual strict $>$ blocking sense

\[
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=65,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
\qquad 
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{65}{58}\approx1.12,
\]

the cheapest strict proportional core forces $N$ to obtain $8\cdot7+9$
approvals whereas the cheapest EJR committee can give $N$ only
$8\cdot6+10$ approvals.

Remark.  With the non-strict $\ge$ formulation of the $s=8$ block the
familiar off-by-one bound $8t+p\ge64$ is obtained, $t=7,p=8,q=5$,
$s_{c}^{\ge}=64$, and the often quoted weak-core ratio is
$64/58=32/29$.  This is the $65\to64$ off-by-one version of the strict
$65/58$ bound above. ∎

$t=|W\cap C|,\quad u_{i}=|W\cap U_{i}|,\quad

$|W|=t+p+q=20$, $0\le u_{i}\le2$, $q\ge4$, 
$|A(9)\cap W|\ge2$, $|A(10)\cap W|\ge2$.

Then for $i\in N$

$v_{i}(W)=|A(i)\cap W|=t+u_{i}$ and

\begin{equation*}
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}v_{i}=8t+p=7t+20-q\; .
\end{equation*}
Put $|S|=s$ and $|X|=2s$.  With $t_{X}=|X\cap C|\le\min\{8,2s\}$ a
strict block of $S\subset N$ is $t_{X}+u_{iX}>t+u_{i}\;\forall i\in S$,
i.e.

\[
\sum_{i\in S}\max \{0,t+u_{i}-t_{X}+1\}\le 2s-t_{X}\; .
\]

For $s\ge4$ the r.h.s. is maximal for $t_{X}=8$ and with
$d_{i}=\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}$

\[
\sum_{i\in S}d_{i}\le 2s-8
\]

is the blocking condition.  In particular for $S=N$

\[
\sum_{i}\max\{0,t+u_{i}-7\}\le 8
\]

blocks $W$.  Hence $t\le6$ is blocked by $N$ and $t\ge7$.

For $t=7$, $d_{i}=u_{i}$ and a strict block of $S$ is
$P_{S}:=\sum_{i\in S}u_{i}\le2s-8$.  Hence a strict $N$-core needs

\[
P_{S}>2s-8\qquad\forall\,|S|=s\ge4,\qquad p=P_{N}>8 .
\]

The cheapest strict realisation is therefore

\[
t_{c}=7,\qquad q_{c}=4,\qquad p_{c}=9,
\]

e.g. $u_{i}=1$ for seven voters and $u_{i}=2$ for one voter,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Then $v_{i}=8$ for seven voters and
$v_{i}=9$ for one voter and $P_{S}>2s-8$ for every $4\le s\le8$, so no

7+u_{i}$.  The often quoted $t=8,p=1,q=11$ point needs

\[

\[
